meta.noteEn: Original questions organised by AET PCP course module (field 'aet'). Not AET's own quiz items. Batch 1: modules 1A, 2A, 6A, 4A, 1B, 4B, 5A.
meta.noteZh: 按 AET PCP 课程模块编排的原创题（字段 aet）。不是学校原题。第一批：1A、2A、6A、4A、1B、4B、5A 七门。

questions.questionEn: A newly graduated PCP in British Columbia asks which organisation actually issues her licence and can attach conditions to it. What is the correct answer?
questions.questionZh: 一名刚毕业的 BC 省 PCP 问：到底是哪个机构给她发执照、并且有权在执照上附加条件？正确答案是什么？

options.en: BC Emergency Health Services, through its clinical governance office
options.zh: BC 紧急医疗服务（BCEHS），通过其临床治理部门

options.en: The Canadian Organization of Paramedic Regulators, which sets the written exam
options.zh: 加拿大护理员监管组织（COPR），因为它出笔试题

options.en: The EMA Licensing Board, under the Emergency Health Services Act
options.zh: 依据《Emergency Health Services Act》设立的 EMA 发牌委员会（EMALB）

options.en: The College of Physicians and Surgeons of BC, via the medical director
options.zh: BC 内外科医师学院，经由医疗总监行使

questions.explanationEn: Under section 6 of the Emergency Health Services Act, the Licensing Board (EMALB) examines, registers and licenses emergency medical assistants, may set terms and conditions on a licence, and investigates complaints. BCEHS is the employer — its Clinical Practice Guidelines govern how you work on the job, but it does not license anyone. COPR administers the PCP entry-to-practice written exam that the Board accepts, but the licence itself comes from EMALB. The College of Physicians and Surgeons regulates physicians, not paramedics.
questions.explanationZh: 依据《Emergency Health Services Act》第 6 条，发牌委员会（EMALB）负责对 EMA 进行考试、注册和发牌，可以为执照设定条款和条件，并调查投诉。BCEHS 是雇主——它的临床实践指南（CPG）规定你上班时怎么做，但它不发执照。COPR 负责主持 Board 认可的 PCP 入职笔试，但执照本身由 EMALB 签发。内外科医师学院管的是医生，不是护理员。

questions.questionEn: A stable patient has a closed, mildly angulated forearm injury with a strong radial pulse and normal sensation, and you are 6 minutes from hospital. Your partner suggests a realignment technique you were shown once and have never performed. You choose to splint in the position found and transport. Which ethical principle most directly guided that decision?
questions.questionZh: 患者病情稳定，前臂闭合性损伤、轻度成角，桡动脉搏动有力、感觉正常，距医院 6 分钟。搭档建议你做一种只见过一次、从未亲手操作过的复位手法。你决定按原位夹板固定后转运。这个决定最直接体现了哪条伦理原则？

options.en: Justice — comparable injuries should receive comparable interventions
options.zh: 公正——同类损伤应得到同类处置

options.en: Non-maleficence — the risk of the manoeuvre outweighs its benefit here
options.zh: 不伤害——这个手法在此情境下风险大于获益

options.en: Autonomy — the patient had not asked for the limb to be realigned
options.zh: 自主——患者并没有要求复位

options.en: Fidelity — keeping faith with your partner's clinical suggestion
options.zh: 忠诚——信守搭档的临床建议

questions.explanationEn: Non-maleficence means avoiding harm. The limb is perfused and only mildly deformed, hospital is minutes away, and the manoeuvre is unpractised — so the realistic risk (pain, neurovascular injury) outweighs any benefit. Under the BC examination guidelines, realignment is reserved for limbs that are grossly deformed or have no distal pulse, so it is not indicated here either. Beneficence would be acting to help; justice is about fair distribution of care, not identical care; autonomy is the patient's right to decide — relevant whenever treatment is offered, but it is not what drove this choice. Fidelity to a colleague is never a reason to perform an unindicated procedure.
questions.explanationZh: 不伤害（non-maleficence）就是避免造成伤害。患肢灌注良好、仅轻度畸形，几分钟就到医院，而且这个手法你从未练过——现实的风险（疼痛、神经血管损伤）大于任何获益。按 BC 考纲，复位只用于严重畸形或远端无脉的肢体，所以这里本来也没有指征。行善（beneficence）是主动去做有益的事；公正（justice）讲的是照护的公平分配，不是人人一样；自主（autonomy）是患者的决定权——只要提供治疗就有关系，但不是本题决定的依据。对搭档的忠诚从来不能成为做无指征操作的理由。

questions.questionEn: Under BC's Emergency Medical Assistants Regulation, which of the following is a condition attached to every EMA licence?
questions.questionZh: 依据 BC 省《Emergency Medical Assistants Regulation》，下列哪一项是附加于每一张 EMA 执照的条件？

options.en: Complying with the Act and regulations, including the Code of Ethics
options.zh: 遵守该法及其法规，包括职业道德准则（Code of Ethics）

options.en: Completing a minimum number of BCEHS shifts in each licence year
options.zh: 每个执照年度为 BCEHS 工作不少于规定班次

options.en: Holding current licences in both the EMR and PCP categories at once
options.zh: 同时持有有效的 EMR 和 PCP 两个类别执照

options.en: Completing a recognised university degree within five years of first licensure
options.zh: 首次发牌后五年内完成认可的大学学位

questions.explanationEn: Section 11 of the Regulation makes compliance with the Act and regulations — including the Schedule 3 Code of Ethics — a condition of every licence, so an ethics breach is also a licence breach the Board can act on. The Regulation does not require employment with BCEHS (many licensees work for other authorised employers), it allows only one licence category at a time (s.8), and there is no degree requirement; a PCP licence runs for five years and is renewed on continuing-competence evidence, not a degree.
questions.explanationZh: 法规第 11 条规定，遵守该法及法规（包括附表 3 的职业道德准则）是每张执照的附带条件，所以违反职业道德同时也是违反执照条件，Board 可以据此处理。法规并不要求必须受雇于 BCEHS（很多持牌人在其他获授权机构工作）；同一时间只能持有一个类别的执照（第 8 条）；也没有学位要求——PCP 执照有效期五年，续牌靠继续能力证明，不靠学位。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic who has held an EMR licence for three years has just passed every PCP examination. She asks whether she can keep the EMR licence active 'as a backup'. What does the EMA Regulation say?
questions.questionZh: 一名持 EMR 执照三年的护理员刚通过全部 PCP 考试。她问能不能把 EMR 执照也留着「以防万一」。《EMA Regulation》怎么规定？

options.en: Yes — a paramedic may hold every category she has qualified for
options.zh: 可以——够资格的类别都可以同时持有

options.en: Yes — provided the EMR licence is renewed on its three-year cycle
options.zh: 可以——只要 EMR 执照按三年周期续牌

options.en: No — the EMR licence becomes an endorsement on the PCP licence
options.zh: 不行——EMR 执照会变成 PCP 执照上的一项背书

options.en: No — the Regulation allows an EMA a licence in only one category at a time
options.zh: 不行——法规规定一名 EMA 同一时间只能持有一个类别的执照

questions.explanationEn: Section 8(1) of the Regulation limits an EMA to one licence category at a time. Nothing is lost: scopes are cumulative, so the PCP Schedule 1 already contains every EMR Schedule 1 and Schedule 2 service. Endorsements are something different — Schedule 2 services (for example CPAP or 12-lead acquisition) added to a licence after approved training, not a previous category folded in. The three-year renewal cycle applies to EMA First Responder licences; EMR and PCP licences run for five years.
questions.explanationZh: 法规第 8(1) 条规定，一名 EMA 同一时间只能持有一个类别的执照。这并不吃亏：执业范围是累加的，PCP 的附表 1 已经包含 EMR 附表 1 和附表 2 的全部服务。背书（endorsement）是另一回事——指完成认可培训后加到执照上的附表 2 服务（比如 CPAP、12 导联采集），不是把原来的类别并进去。三年一续的是 EMA First Responder 执照；EMR 和 PCP 执照有效期都是五年。

questions.questionEn: Two months after moving to a new apartment and transferring to a different station, a PCP realises he never told the Licensing Board. What does the EMA Regulation require?
questions.questionZh: 一名 PCP 搬了新家、又调去另一个站，两个月后才想起从没通知过发牌委员会。《EMA Regulation》要求他怎么做？

options.en: Nothing further — the employer updates the register on his behalf
options.zh: 不用再做什么——雇主会替他更新注册簿

options.en: Notify the Board in writing now; the 30-day deadline has already passed
options.zh: 立即书面通知 Board；30 天期限已经过了

options.en: Report the changes at his next five-year renewal, as the Regulation allows
options.zh: 按法规允许，等下次五年续牌时一并申报

options.en: Apply for a new licence, because the register entry is now invalid
options.zh: 重新申请执照，因为注册记录已经失效

questions.explanationEn: Section 13(2) of the Regulation puts the duty on the licensee: notify the Board in writing within 30 days of a change of name, address or place of employment, because the register must show where each EMA works and how to reach them. The employer does not do this for you. The licence itself remains valid — it is not voided by the lapse — but he is out of compliance with a licence condition until he notifies, so the fix is to do it now, not at renewal.
questions.explanationZh: 法规第 13(2) 条把义务放在持牌人自己身上：姓名、地址或工作单位变更后 30 天内书面通知 Board，因为注册簿必须记载每名 EMA 的工作地点和联系方式。雇主不会替你做这件事。执照本身仍然有效——不会因为漏报而作废——但在补报之前他一直处于违反执照条件的状态，所以应该现在就补，而不是等续牌。

questions.questionEn: A 78-year-old woman you have treated several times for COPD offers to pay you to drive her to specialist appointments on your days off, saying she trusts you more than the taxi service. What is the most appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 一位 78 岁的 COPD 患者，你出诊接触过她好几次。她提出付钱请你休息日开车送她去看专科，说比起出租车她更信任你。最恰当的回应是什么？

options.en: Accept, but charge only enough to cover fuel so it is not a business
options.zh: 答应，但只收油费，这样就不算做生意

options.en: Accept without any payment, since helping people is simply part of being a paramedic
options.zh: 答应但分文不收，因为帮助别人本来就是护理员的本分

options.en: Decline kindly, explain the boundary, and point her to transport resources
options.zh: 婉拒，说明职业边界，并给她指出交通资源

options.en: Agree to one trip, then ask your supervisor whether it can continue
options.zh: 先答应送一次，再问主管以后能不能继续

questions.explanationEn: This is a dual relationship: you would be her paramedic and her private driver, with money and personal loyalty mixed into a relationship that depends on a power imbalance and clinical objectivity. Removing the fee does not remove the boundary problem, and 'just once' still crosses it before anyone has reviewed it. The professional answer protects the relationship by redirecting her to services built for the need — accessible transit such as HandyDART, bc211 (2-1-1) for community transport programs, or community paramedicine where it exists — and, if appropriate, flagging the gap to your service.
questions.explanationZh: 这是一种双重关系：你既是她的护理员，又成了她的私人司机，把金钱和私人情分掺进了一段本来依赖权力不对等和临床客观性的关系。不收钱并不能消除边界问题；「就送一次」也是先越了界再说。专业的做法是把需求引向为此而设的服务——无障碍交通（如 HandyDART）、bc211（拨 2-1-1）查询社区接送项目、有条件的地区可转介社区护理员（community paramedicine）——必要时把这个服务缺口反映给你的机构，这样反而保护了这段关系。

questions.questionEn: Reviewing a shared call, you notice your partner's PCR lists three complete sets of vital signs. You were with the patient throughout and know only one set was taken. He shrugs: 'Everyone pads the vitals — it protects us.' What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 复盘一次共同出诊时，你发现搭档写的 PCR 上有三组完整生命体征。你全程都在患者身边，清楚只量过一组。他耸耸肩：「大家都往上补体征，这是保护我们自己。」你该怎么做？

options.en: Ask him to correct it; if he refuses, report it through the service's process
options.zh: 要求他更正；若他拒绝，就按机构流程举报

options.en: Say nothing — the PCR is his legal document and his responsibility alone
options.zh: 什么都不说——PCR 是他的法律文书，责任只在他

options.en: Add a note to your own copy recording the true number of vital-sign sets
options.zh: 在自己留存的副本上加备注，写明真实的体征组数

options.en: Describe the incident anonymously on a paramedic discussion forum to raise awareness
options.zh: 匿名发到护理员讨论论坛上，提醒大家注意

questions.explanationEn: Recording vital signs that were never taken is falsification of a legal record — in BC it can end a licence, and it endangers the patient because downstream clinicians will trust a trend that never existed. The Schedule 3 Code of Ethics obliges every EMA to perform duties with integrity and to report incompetent, illegal or unethical conduct of colleagues to the appropriate authority; it also forbids disparaging colleagues, which is why the route is a direct conversation and then the service's formal process — not gossip or a public forum post that may breach patient privacy. Staying silent makes you part of it, and a private note does nothing to fix the record the hospital relies on.
questions.explanationZh: 把没量过的生命体征写进记录，就是伪造法律文书——在 BC 这足以丢掉执照，而且会危及患者，因为后续的医护会相信一条根本不存在的趋势。附表 3 职业道德准则要求每名 EMA 诚信履职，并向有关当局举报同事不胜任、非法或不道德的行为；准则同时禁止诋毁同事，所以正确路径是先当面谈、再走机构的正式流程——而不是传闲话或发到公开论坛（还可能泄露患者隐私）。沉默等于参与，自己留备注也改变不了医院依赖的那份记录。

questions.questionEn: A national resuscitation guideline published this month recommends changing the sequence of a protocol you use. Your BCEHS Clinical Practice Guideline has not changed, and neither have the BC examination guidelines. How should this affect your practice on tomorrow's shift?
questions.questionZh: 本月新发布的一份全国复苏指南建议修改你正在用的某个流程的顺序。你的 BCEHS 临床实践指南没有变，BC 考纲也没有变。这对你明天上班的做法应该有什么影响？

options.en: Adopt the new national sequence at once — the newest evidence takes precedence
options.zh: 马上改用全国新顺序——最新证据优先

options.en: Use the new sequence only for patients who agree to the newer approach
options.zh: 只对同意用新方法的患者采用新顺序

options.en: Disregard national guidelines entirely; they do not apply in BC
options.zh: 完全不理会全国指南，它们在 BC 不适用

options.en: Follow the current CPG for now and raise the new evidence through clinical governance
options.zh: 暂时继续按现行 CPG 执行，把新证据提交临床治理渠道

questions.explanationEn: Knowledge translation runs in steps: research becomes a national guideline, which a medical director then adapts into a local Clinical Practice Guideline that accounts for BC law, scope of practice, equipment and resources. Until that local step happens, the CPG you are authorised to follow is the current one, and the licensing exam marks against the BC examination guidelines. National guidelines matter — they are exactly what you should feed into the review process — but a patient's agreement cannot authorise a change outside your protocols, and ignoring national evidence entirely is the opposite of continuing competence.
questions.explanationZh: 知识转化是分步走的：研究先变成全国指南，再由医疗总监结合 BC 的法律、执业范围、设备和资源改编成本地临床实践指南（CPG）。在本地这一步完成之前，你获授权执行的仍是现行 CPG，而执照考试按 BC 考纲评分。全国指南很重要——它正是你应该递交给审核流程的材料——但患者同意不能授权你在流程之外改动做法，完全无视全国证据则与继续能力的要求背道而驰。

questions.questionEn: A protocol step would delay transport of a patient who is deteriorating quickly, and the protocol's listed indications do not quite match what you are seeing. Online medical oversight is available by phone. What is the most defensible course of action?
questions.questionZh: 某流程中的一步会耽误一位病情迅速恶化患者的转运，而且该流程列出的指征和你眼前的情况不完全吻合。可以电话联系在线医疗指导。最站得住脚的做法是什么？

options.en: Carry out the protocol step exactly as written; deviation is never permitted
options.zh: 一字不差地执行那一步；任何偏离都不允许

options.en: Treat the patient's immediate needs, call medical oversight, and document both steps
options.zh: 先处理患者的紧急需求，电话请医疗指导，并把两步都记录在案

options.en: Skip the step and leave it out of the PCR so that it does not raise questions
options.zh: 跳过那一步，PCR 里不写，以免招来质疑

options.en: Ask the family to choose which approach they would prefer you to take
options.zh: 让家属选择他们更想要哪种做法

questions.explanationEn: Protocols are preset algorithms written for typical presentations; when the indications do not fit or following a step would harm the patient, the accountable response is to act on the patient's immediate needs within your scope, obtain direction from medical oversight (in BCEHS practice the CliniCall / emergency physician line), and record both your reasoning and the advice. That record is what makes the decision defensible. Hiding a deviation from the PCR turns a judgment call into falsification, and family preference cannot substitute for clinical direction. In the AET course this is taught as clinical judgment plus documentation; on the EMALB practical exam, apply the BC protocols as written — including checking indications and contraindications — unless the examiner directs otherwise.
questions.explanationZh: 流程是针对典型表现预设的算法；当指征不吻合、或者照做某一步会伤害患者时，负责任的做法是在执业范围内先处理患者的紧急需求，向医疗指导取得指示（BCEHS 实际执业中是 CliniCall / 急诊医生热线），并把你的推理和得到的建议一并记录下来——这份记录正是决定站得住脚的依据。把偏离藏起来不写进 PCR，就把一次判断变成了造假；家属的偏好也不能替代临床指导。AET 课上把这教成「临床判断 + 记录」；在 EMALB 实操考试里，除非考官另有指示，否则按 BC 流程原样执行——包括核对指征和禁忌。

questions.questionEn: Which statement correctly describes the continuing-competence requirement for a licensed PCP in British Columbia?
questions.questionZh: 关于 BC 省持牌 PCP 的继续能力（continuing competence）要求，下列哪项说法正确？

options.en: 40 classroom hours every five years, reported with the renewal application
options.zh: 每五年 40 小时课堂培训，随续牌申请一并申报

options.en: 10 continuing-education credits a year, with no patient-contact requirement
options.zh: 每年 10 个继续教育学分，不要求患者接触次数

options.en: 20 CE credits and 20 patient contacts per year, reported online by April 30
options.zh: 每年 20 个继续教育学分加 20 次患者接触，4 月 30 日前在线申报

options.en: A written re-examination every year, scheduled by the Licensing Board
options.zh: 每年由发牌委员会安排重新参加一次笔试

questions.explanationEn: Part 4 of the EMA Regulation sets an annual cycle: the reporting period runs April 1 to March 31, and in each period a PCP needs at least 20 CE credits plus at least 20 patient contacts, reported through the ministry's website by April 30. If contacts fall short, surplus CE credits substitute one-for-one. Supporting documents must be kept for three years. A written or practical evaluating exam is only imposed if the director finds you non-compliant — it is not a routine yearly requirement. The five-year figure is the licence term, not a training block.
questions.explanationZh: 《EMA Regulation》第 4 部分规定的是年度周期：报告周期为 4 月 1 日至次年 3 月 31 日，每个周期内 PCP 需要至少 20 个继续教育学分加至少 20 次患者接触，并在 4 月 30 日前通过卫生厅网站申报。患者接触不够时，多出来的学分可以一比一抵扣。支持文件要保存三年。只有在 director 认定你未达标时才会被要求参加评估考试（笔试或实操）——那不是每年的例行要求。「五年」是执照有效期，不是培训时段。

questions.questionEn: You read a single observational study from a large US city in which ALS crews with physician backup reported better outcomes using a technique that is outside BC PCP scope. A colleague wants your rural crew to start using it. What is the best response?
questions.questionZh: 你读到一篇来自美国大城市的单项观察性研究：有医生支援的 ALS 车组用一种超出 BC PCP 执业范围的技术取得了更好的结局。一位同事想让你们的乡村车组也用起来。最好的回应是什么？

options.en: Note the setting and scope differ, and refer the paper to clinical governance
options.zh: 指出场景和执业范围都不同，把论文交给临床治理讨论

options.en: Begin using the technique right away — a published study is sufficient authorisation
options.zh: 马上开始使用——有发表的研究就足以作为授权

options.en: Dismiss the study outright because it was not conducted in Canada
options.zh: 因为不是在加拿大做的，直接否定这项研究

options.en: Use the technique only on patients who are unlikely to complain afterwards
options.zh: 只对事后不太会投诉的患者使用

questions.explanationEn: Critical appraisal asks two questions: is the study believable, and does it apply to my patients and my system? One observational study cannot prove cause and effect, and an urban ALS service with physician support is a very different setting from a rural BC PCP crew — different providers, equipment and transport times. On top of that, a journal article cannot expand your licence: the services you may provide are set by Schedule 1 and Schedule 2 of the EMA Regulation and your employer's guidelines. Rejecting a study purely because of its country is not appraisal, and selecting patients by their likelihood to complain is unethical.
questions.explanationZh: 批判性评读要问两个问题：这项研究可信吗？它适用于我的患者和我的系统吗？一项观察性研究证明不了因果；有医生支援的城市 ALS 服务，和 BC 乡村 PCP 车组是完全不同的场景——人员、设备、转运时间都不同。何况一篇论文不能扩大你的执照范围：你能提供的服务由《EMA Regulation》附表 1、附表 2 和雇主的指南决定。仅因国别就否定研究不是评读；按「会不会投诉」挑患者则是不道德的。

questions.questionEn: After a difficult airway call you want to add an entry to your CPD portfolio that would stand up in an audit. Which entry is strongest?
questions.questionZh: 一次棘手的气道出诊后，你想往 CPD 档案里加一条经得起审计的记录。哪一条最有力？

options.en: 'Attended the regional airway refresher workshop, 3 hours, certificate of attendance attached.'
options.zh: 「参加地区气道复训工作坊，3 小时，出席证书附后。」

options.en: 'Difficult airway call today; felt terrible about how it went and will try to do better.'
options.zh: 「今天的气道出诊很棘手，对过程感觉很糟，以后会努力做得更好。」

options.en: 'Airway refresher completed on schedule — see attached certificate, agenda and sign-in sheet.'
options.zh: 「气道复训按时完成——见附件证书、议程和签到表。」

options.en: 'Airway refresher, 3 h: gap = one-hand BVM seal; now using two-hand seal; recheck in 60 days.'
options.zh: 「气道复训 3 小时：短板 = 单手 BVM 密封；已改用双手密封；60 天后复查。」

questions.explanationEn: An audit-ready CPD entry closes the loop: what the activity was, what you learned, how it changed your practice, and how you will check it stuck. That is also what the EMA Regulation asks you to record for each CE activity — date, duration, location, description, and the knowledge or skills attained. A certificate or an hours figure proves attendance, not learning, and a purely emotional note has no learning need, action or follow-up, so neither would satisfy a reviewer.
questions.explanationZh: 经得起审计的 CPD 记录要闭环：活动是什么、学到了什么、怎样改变了你的做法、以及如何验证效果保持住了。《EMA Regulation》对每项继续教育活动要求记录的也正是这些——日期、时长、地点、描述，以及获得的知识或技能。证书或小时数只能证明出席，不能证明学到了；纯情绪化的一句话既没有学习需求、也没有行动和跟进，审核的人都不会认可。

questions.questionEn: Which PCR entry best meets the standard of objective, defensible documentation for a man found sitting on the floor of a pub?
questions.questionZh: 一名男性被发现坐在酒吧地板上。下列哪条 PCR 记录最符合客观、经得起质疑的书写标准？

options.en: 'Pt obviously intoxicated and uncooperative; most likely seeking a bed for the night, no acute medical issue.'
options.zh: 「患者明显醉酒、不配合；多半只是想找张床过夜，没有急性医疗问题。」

options.en: 'Pt assessed, appeared well and in no distress; nothing significant found on examination.'
options.zh: 「已评估患者，看起来状态好、无痛苦；查体未见明显异常。」

options.en: 'Pt states "I had four beers." Slurred speech, unsteady gait, odour of alcohol. BGL 5.8 mmol/L. GCS 14 (E4 V4 M6).'
options.zh: 「患者自述『我喝了四瓶啤酒』。言语含糊、步态不稳、有酒味。BGL 5.8 mmol/L。GCS 14（E4 V4 M6）。」

options.en: 'Pt intoxicated, alcohol level high, refused all care and transport; left in care of bar staff.'
options.zh: 「患者醉酒，酒精浓度很高，拒绝一切处置和转运；交由酒吧员工照看。」

questions.explanationEn: Good documentation records what you saw, measured and were told — in the patient's own words where it matters — and leaves the conclusions to the reader. The strong entry quotes the patient, lists observable signs, gives a measured glucose (showing hypoglycemia was ruled out before anything was attributed to alcohol) and a scored GCS. The entry calling him 'intoxicated' and 'uncooperative' is opinion that would embarrass you in court and could anchor the next clinician's thinking. 'Appeared well' with nothing measured is too vague to defend. 'Alcohol level high' asserts a measurement you never took, and 'refused all care' records a refusal with none of the detail (what was offered, what was explained) that would make it valid.
questions.explanationZh: 好的记录写的是你看到的、量到的、听到的——关键处引用患者原话——把结论留给读者去下。那条规范的记录引用了患者的话，列出可观察的体征，给出测得的血糖（说明在把问题归因于酒精之前先排除了低血糖），还有逐项计分的 GCS。写「醉酒、不配合」是主观评价，上了法庭会让你难堪，还会把下一位医护的思路带偏。「看起来状态好」却没有任何测量值，太空泛，经不起追问。「酒精浓度很高」声称了一个你根本没测的数值；「拒绝一切处置」只写了拒绝，却没有让拒绝成立的任何细节（提供了什么、解释了什么）。

questions.questionEn: While completing a paper PCR you write the wrong time beside a nitroglycerin dose. How should the error be corrected?
questions.questionZh: 填写纸质 PCR 时，你在一次硝酸甘油给药旁边写错了时间。应该怎样更正？

options.en: Single line through the error, correct time beside it, your initials and the date
options.zh: 错误处划一条单线，旁边写上正确时间，签姓名缩写和日期

options.en: Cover the error with correction fluid, then write the correct time neatly over the top
options.zh: 用涂改液盖掉错误，再在上面工整地写上正确时间

options.en: Black out the entry completely and rewrite the whole treatment section
options.zh: 把那一条彻底涂黑，整个处置部分重写

options.en: Discard the page and start a fresh PCR, without mentioning the error
options.zh: 把这页作废，重新写一份 PCR，不提这个错误

questions.explanationEn: A PCR is a legal record, and the test for any correction is transparency: a reader must be able to see what was written first, what replaced it, who changed it and when. A single ruled line with initials and date does exactly that. Correction fluid or heavy scribbling hides the original and looks like tampering if the record is ever examined in a complaint or court case. Throwing the page away breaks the chain of the record. Electronic PCRs handle this through an amendment or addendum that is logged in the audit trail — the same principle, enforced by the software.
questions.explanationZh: PCR 是法律文书，任何更正的标准都是透明：读的人必须能看出最初写了什么、改成了什么、谁改的、什么时候改的。划一条单线并签缩写和日期正是如此。涂改液或大面积涂黑会掩盖原文，一旦记录在投诉或诉讼中被调阅，就像是在做手脚。把那页扔掉则破坏了记录的完整链条。电子 PCR 通过带审计记录的修订或补充条目来处理——原理相同，只是由软件强制执行。

questions.questionEn: After offloading a hypoglycemic patient you realise you never documented the repeat blood glucose of 6.1 mmol/L that you measured at 14:32. The PCR was submitted at 14:50; it is now 15:10. How should the information be added?
questions.questionZh: 送完一位低血糖患者后，你发现 14:32 复测的血糖 6.1 mmol/L 根本没写进去。PCR 已于 14:50 提交，现在是 15:10。应该怎样补上这条信息？

options.en: Enter the value on the 14:32 line so that the record reads as if it had always been there
options.zh: 把数值填进 14:32 那一行，让记录看起来本来就有

options.en: Add a labelled late entry showing 15:10 as written, 14:32 as measured, and the value
options.zh: 做一条标注的补记：写明补记时间 15:10、测量时间 14:32 和数值

options.en: Leave it out — a submitted PCR cannot be altered, so the omission stands
options.zh: 不补了——已提交的 PCR 不能再改，漏了就漏了

options.en: Tell the receiving nurse verbally and leave the written record as it is
options.zh: 口头告诉接收护士，书面记录保持原样

questions.explanationEn: Late entries are legitimate as long as they are honest about being late. Labelling the addendum with both the time you are writing and the time the event happened preserves the true sequence and shows nothing was back-dated. Quietly inserting the value into the original timeline is falsification, even though the number is real. Records can be amended after submission — that is what addendum processes exist for — and a verbal message to one nurse leaves no trace for the clinicians who read the chart later. The repeat glucose also matters clinically: it is the evidence that the treatment worked.
questions.explanationZh: 补记是合规的，前提是坦白它是补记。在补充条目里同时写明补记时间和事件实际发生时间，既保住了真实的先后顺序，也表明没有倒填日期。悄悄把数值塞进原来的时间线，即使数字是真的，也属于伪造。记录提交后是可以修订的——补充条目流程就是为此而设；只口头告诉一位护士，后面看病历的医护什么都查不到。这个复测血糖在临床上也很重要：它是治疗有效的证据。

questions.questionEn: Without the patient's explicit consent, to which of the following may a paramedic disclose clinical information from a call?
questions.questionZh: 在没有患者明确同意的情况下，护理员可以把出诊的临床信息透露给下列哪一方？

options.en: The patient's employer, who phones to ask why the employee missed work
options.zh: 患者的雇主，打电话来问员工为什么没上班

options.en: A journalist writing about ambulance response times in that neighbourhood
options.zh: 正在写该社区救护车响应时间报道的记者

options.en: A neighbour who says she is 'practically family' and will check on him
options.zh: 自称「跟家人差不多」、会去看他的邻居

options.en: The emergency department staff taking over the patient's care
options.zh: 正在接手患者照护的急诊科工作人员

questions.explanationEn: Information collected to care for a patient may be shared with the clinicians who continue that care — the receiving ED team is inside the circle of care, and the hand-off report is exactly this kind of disclosure. The Code of Ethics tells EMAs to preserve the confidence of patient information consistent with acting for the patient's well-being, and BC's Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act limits a public body such as BCEHS to using personal information for the purpose it was collected or a consistent purpose. An employer, a reporter or a neighbour has no such role; even confirming that you attended a particular address is personal information. They need the patient's consent or a legal authority.
questions.explanationZh: 为照护患者而收集的信息，可以与继续这段照护的医护共享——接收的急诊团队属于照护圈（circle of care），交接报告本身就是这类披露。职业道德准则要求 EMA 在以患者福祉为准则的前提下保守患者信息的机密；BC《信息自由与隐私保护法》（FOIPPA）也限定像 BCEHS 这样的公共机构只能为收集时的目的或与之一致的目的使用个人信息。雇主、记者、邻居都没有这种角色；哪怕只是证实你去过某个地址，也属于个人信息。他们需要患者同意或法律授权。

questions.questionEn: At a two-car collision a police officer asks you for the driver's blood glucose reading, what he told you about drinking, and a copy of your PCR 'for the file'. The driver is alert and has not consented. What is the correct approach?
questions.questionZh: 两车相撞现场，警察向你索要司机的血糖读数、他跟你说的饮酒情况，以及一份 PCR 复印件「留档」。司机神志清楚，没有同意。正确做法是什么？

options.en: Hand over the PCR copy — a request from police must be met on the spot
options.zh: 把 PCR 复印件给他——警察的要求必须当场满足

options.en: Share scene-safety facts only; refer the clinical request to the formal process
options.zh: 只说现场安全相关的事实；临床信息的索要转到正式流程

options.en: Refuse to speak with the officer about anything at all, including hazards on scene
options.zh: 完全拒绝和警官谈任何事，包括现场的危险因素

options.en: Give the clinical details verbally but decline to provide the paper copy
options.zh: 口头告知临床细节，但不给纸质复印件

questions.explanationEn: A police officer's interest does not by itself create a right to a patient's clinical information. Under BC's privacy legislation a public body may disclose personal information to law enforcement only in defined circumstances — for example to comply with a warrant, subpoena or court order, or where disclosure is clearly necessary for someone's safety — and ambulance services route such requests through a formal process so the decision is made and recorded properly. Saying it out loud is still a disclosure, so the verbal-only option is no better than the paper copy. Scene safety is different: hazards, weapons or an aggressive bystander should be shared freely. Separate statutory reporting duties (for example child protection) are covered in the mandatory-reporting module, not by an informal roadside request.
questions.explanationZh: 警察感兴趣，本身并不构成获取患者临床信息的权利。按 BC 的隐私立法，公共机构只能在特定情形下向执法部门披露个人信息——例如为了执行搜查令、传票或法院命令，或者披露对某人的安全明显必要——救护服务会把这类请求导入正式流程，让决定有人负责、有据可查。口头说出来同样是披露，所以「只说不给纸」并不比给复印件好。现场安全是另一回事：危险因素、武器、有攻击性的旁观者应该主动告知。法定的报告义务（如儿童保护）属于强制报告那一模块的内容，不是路边一句非正式的索要就能触发的。

questions.questionEn: You want the receiving physician to appreciate a dramatic wound before you cover it with a dressing. Which action respects the patient's privacy?
questions.questionZh: 你想让接收医生在你覆盖敷料前看到一处触目惊心的伤口。哪种做法尊重患者隐私？

options.en: Photograph it on your personal phone and text the picture directly to the physician
options.zh: 用自己的手机拍下来，直接短信发给医生

options.en: Post it in the crew's group chat with the face cropped out, for teaching
options.zh: 裁掉脸部后发到车组群里，用作教学

options.en: Describe it in detail; use an approved secure device only if an image is needed
options.zh: 详细描述记录；确需影像时只用机构批准的安全设备

options.en: Photograph it, show the physician, then delete the image so no record exists
options.zh: 拍下来给医生看，然后删掉，不留任何记录

questions.explanationEn: A photograph of a patient is personal health information. Taking it on a personal phone places it outside the public body's control — backed up to a cloud account, visible in notifications, impossible for the service to audit or protect as privacy law requires. A group chat adds unauthorised recipients, and cropping the face does not de-identify a distinctive injury. Deleting the image afterwards does not undo the unauthorised collection and could be viewed as destroying a record. A precise written description plus a clear hand-off does the clinical job; where imaging is truly needed, services provide an approved, encrypted and logged route.
questions.explanationZh: 患者照片属于个人健康信息。用私人手机拍摄，信息就脱离了公共机构的控制——会同步到云端账号、在通知栏里显示，机构无法按隐私法要求审计和保护。发到群里等于增加了未经授权的接收者，裁掉脸也无法让一处特征明显的伤口去识别化。事后删除并不能抵消未经授权的收集，还可能被视为销毁记录。精确的文字描述加清楚的交接足以完成临床任务；确实需要影像时，机构有批准的、加密并留痕的渠道。

questions.questionEn: In the EMALB practical examination, which statement about the patient care report is correct?
questions.questionZh: 关于 EMALB 实操考试中的患者护理记录（PCR），下列哪项正确？

options.en: 5 minutes to submit the PCR; leaving out critical information is a moderate deficiency
options.zh: 5 分钟内提交 PCR；遗漏关键信息按中度缺陷扣分

options.en: The PCR becomes optional whenever the verbal hand-off report was judged complete
options.zh: 只要口头交接被认定完整，PCR 就可以不写

options.en: Only the vital signs are reviewed; history fields are not graded
options.zh: 只审核生命体征，病史栏目不计分

options.en: Missing three or more relevant data fields is graded the same as missing one
options.zh: 缺三个及以上相关栏目和只缺一个栏目扣分相同

questions.explanationEn: The BC examination guidelines give the candidate 5 minutes to complete and submit the PCR, and the marking scheme classes failure to provide critical information in a record or report as a moderate deficiency (non-critical but pertinent omissions are minor). The documentation component takes deductions for not submitting a PCR, an illegible PCR, missing significant data fields (three or more is the example given), data that does not match the scenario — such as medications or allergies recorded differently from what the patient said — and minor gaps of one or two fields. The examiner's focus when reading the PCR is the history (chief complaint, history of chief complaint, past medical history, medications, allergies), vital signs, treatments and relevant findings — so history fields are very much graded.
questions.explanationZh: BC 考纲给考生 5 分钟完成并提交 PCR；评分标准把「记录或报告中遗漏关键信息」归为中度缺陷（遗漏非关键但相关的信息是轻度缺陷）。文书部分的扣分点包括：没有提交 PCR、字迹无法辨认、遗漏重要数据栏目（标准举例是三个及以上）、记录与情景不符——比如用药或过敏写得和患者说的不一样——以及只缺一两个栏目的小瑕疵。考官审 PCR 时的重点是病史（主诉、现病史、既往史、用药、过敏）、生命体征、处置和相关发现——所以病史栏目当然计分。

questions.questionEn: In a crowded hospital elevator your partner starts recounting the last call: 'That diabetic on Elm Street with the pit bull — second overdose this month.' No name is mentioned. What is the right response?
questions.questionZh: 在挤满人的医院电梯里，搭档开始讲刚才那单：「榆树街那个养比特犬的糖尿病人——这个月第二次过量了。」没提名字。正确的回应是什么？

options.en: Nothing — without a name, no private information has actually been shared
options.zh: 不用管——没说名字就不算泄露任何隐私

options.en: Correct the street name so that at least the story is told accurately
options.zh: 纠正一下街名，至少把事情讲准确

options.en: Join in — an elevator inside a health-care facility is a clinical setting
options.zh: 一起聊——医院里的电梯本来就是临床场所

options.en: Stop the conversation and continue it somewhere private
options.zh: 打住，换到私密场合再谈

questions.explanationEn: Privacy law protects information about an identifiable person, and identification does not require a name: a street, a distinctive dog, a diagnosis and a pattern of calls together point to one household, and a visitor in that elevator may well be a neighbour. A hospital elevator is a public space. The Code of Ethics duty to preserve the confidence of patient information applies to casual talk just as much as to records. Clinical discussion between partners is legitimate — in the cab of the ambulance or a staff-only room, not in a lift full of strangers.
questions.explanationZh: 隐私法保护的是「可识别个人」的信息，而识别并不需要名字：一条街、一只特征明显的狗、一个诊断、再加上多次呼叫的模式，合起来就指向一户人家，电梯里的某位探视者很可能就是邻居。医院电梯是公共空间。职业道德准则中保守患者信息机密的义务，对闲聊和对记录同样适用。搭档之间讨论病例是正当的——在救护车驾驶室或员工专用房间里，而不是在挤满陌生人的电梯里。

questions.questionEn: You gave salbutamol 5 mg by nebuliser at 10:05 and repeated it at 10:20. Your PCR reads: 'Ventolin neb x2, pt better.' Why does this entry fall short?
questions.questionZh: 你在 10:05 雾化给了沙丁胺醇 5 mg，10:20 重复了一次。PCR 上写的是：「Ventolin 雾化 ×2，患者好转。」这条记录为什么不合格？

options.en: Nothing — the drug and the patient's response are both documented
options.zh: 并不缺什么——药物和患者反应都写了

options.en: Only the name is wrong; 'salbutamol' should replace the trade name
options.zh: 只是名字不对，应该把商品名换成「沙丁胺醇」

options.en: Each dose needs the drug, dose, route, time and measured response
options.zh: 每一剂都要写药名、剂量、途径、时间和客观反应

options.en: The second dose should not appear; repeats under protocol are implied
options.zh: 第二剂不该写；按流程重复给药是不言自明的

questions.explanationEn: 'Right documentation' is one of the rights of medication administration, and in the BC practical exam it is scored in the records-and-reports component — drug timings are recorded from the time of the original administration, and every repeat is a separate timed entry. The entry gives no dose, no route, no times and a subjective 'better' instead of measurable change (SpO₂ before and after, respiratory rate, air entry, ability to speak). Without that, the ED cannot judge how much bronchodilator the patient has already had or whether he is actually improving. The five elements the AET course teaches for handing over a medication (what was given, how much, by which route, when, and what it did) are the same checklist spoken aloud. Trade versus generic name is a minor issue by comparison; implied doses are never acceptable.
questions.explanationZh: 「正确记录」是给药诸项「正确」之一，在 BC 实操考试里计入记录与报告部分——给药时间以首次给药时刻为准，每一次重复都要单独记时间。这条记录没有剂量、没有途径、没有时间，只有一个主观的「好转」，而不是可测量的变化（给药前后的 SpO₂、呼吸频率、呼吸音、能否成句说话）。缺了这些，急诊无法判断患者已经用了多少支气管扩张剂、是否真的在改善。AET 课上的五要素用药交接——药名、剂量、途径、时间、反应——就是同一张清单的口头版。相比之下商品名还是通用名只是小问题；「不言自明」的剂量永远不可接受。

questions.questionEn: A patient you transported last week phones the station asking for a copy of 'everything you wrote about me'. What is the appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 上周你转运过的一位患者打电话到站里，要一份「你写我的所有东西」的复印件。恰当的回应是什么？

options.en: Read your copy to her over the phone — it is her own information
options.zh: 在电话里把你那份念给她听——反正是她自己的信息

options.en: Direct her to the service's formal access-to-records process
options.zh: 引导她走机构的正式记录查阅流程

options.en: Refuse — ambulance records belong to the service and are never released
options.zh: 拒绝——救护记录属于机构，从不对外提供

options.en: Scan your copy and email it to the address she gives you over the phone
options.zh: 把你那份扫描后发到她电话里给的邮箱

questions.explanationEn: Under BC's Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act, individuals have a right of access to their own personal information held by a public body, so a flat refusal is wrong. But the right is exercised through the organisation's access process, not through whoever answers the station phone: the office confirms the caller really is the patient, removes third-party information that may be in the record, and logs the release. Reading the record to an unverified voice, or emailing it to an unverified address, risks handing a stranger someone else's health information.
questions.explanationZh: 依据 BC《信息自由与隐私保护法》，个人有权查阅公共机构持有的本人个人信息，所以一口回绝是错的。但这项权利要通过机构的信息查阅流程来行使，而不是由谁接了站里电话谁来办：相关部门会核实来电者确实是患者本人、去除记录中可能涉及的第三方信息，并对发放留痕。对着一个未经核实的声音念记录，或者发到一个未经核实的邮箱，都有把别人的健康信息交到陌生人手里的风险。

questions.questionEn: A classmate says: 'Either you're born tough enough for this job or you're not.' Which reply best reflects what is known about resilience in paramedics?
questions.questionZh: 一位同学说：「这行要么天生够硬，要么就干不了。」哪句回应最符合目前对护理员心理韧性的认识？

options.en: 'It's built from skills and supports you can learn, and it changes over a career.'
options.zh: 「它是靠可以学的技能和支持建立起来的，而且一辈子都会变化。」

options.en: 'True — genuinely resilient people simply do not have stress reactions after calls.'
options.zh: 「没错——真正有韧性的人出诊之后根本不会有应激反应。」

options.en: 'Resilience mostly means keeping your feelings to yourself so the crew stays steady.'
options.zh: 「韧性主要是把情绪憋在心里，别影响车组的稳定。」

options.en: 'It's fixed by your early twenties, so there is little point in working on it now.'
options.zh: 「二十出头就定型了，现在再练也没多大意义。」

questions.explanationEn: Resilience is the process of adapting well under adversity, and the research on first responders treats it as modifiable: protective sleep, physical activity, social connection, meaning-making and early help-seeking all strengthen it, and it fluctuates with workload and life events. Having a stress reaction after a distressing call is normal and expected — recovery, not immunity, is the marker. Suppressing emotion is one of the coping styles consistently linked with worse outcomes, and the 'fixed trait' view discourages exactly the habits that protect people over a long career.
questions.explanationZh: 韧性是在逆境中良好适应的过程，针对一线急救人员的研究把它视为可以改变的：保护性睡眠、体力活动、社交联结、找到意义感、及早求助都能增强它，而且它会随工作负荷和生活事件起伏。令人难受的出诊之后出现应激反应是正常、可以预期的——标志是恢复，而不是免疫。压抑情绪是被反复证实与较差结局相关的应对方式之一；「天生定型」的看法恰恰会让人放弃那些能在漫长职业生涯中保护自己的习惯。

questions.questionEn: You are rostered for a 12-hour shift starting at 06:00. You were up most of the night with a sick child and slept about two hours; on the drive in you catch yourself drifting and cannot remember the last few kilometres. What should you do before taking the ambulance out?
questions.questionZh: 你排了早上 6 点开始的 12 小时班。夜里照顾生病的孩子几乎没睡，只睡了约两小时；开车上班途中你发现自己走神，想不起刚才那几公里是怎么开过来的。出车前你该怎么做？

options.en: Drink two energy drinks and start the shift — the roster depends on you
options.zh: 灌两罐能量饮料直接上班——排班就靠你了

options.en: Say nothing, and ask your partner to do all of the driving today
options.zh: 什么都不说，让搭档今天全程开车

options.en: Take the first few calls and reassess yourself at the mid-shift break
options.zh: 先接几单，到中途休息时再看看自己状态

options.en: Tell the supervisor you are unfit for duty right now and ask to be stood down
options.zh: 告诉主管你现在不适合上岗，请求停勤

questions.explanationEn: Fitness to practise is the individual's responsibility before it is anyone else's. Two hours of sleep plus a lapse of attention at the wheel is already evidence of impairment, and fatigue of this degree degrades judgement, drug calculation and reaction time in the same way alcohol does. Letting your partner drive fixes nothing about your clinical decisions; stimulants mask sleepiness without restoring performance; and 'see how it goes' means the first patients are the test. Reporting to the supervisor is the professional act — the Code of Ethics puts the patient's well-being above all, and services have fatigue policies precisely so that a crew member can be stood down without blame.
questions.explanationZh: 是否适合上岗，首先是你自己的责任。只睡两小时加上开车时注意力中断，本身就是能力受损的证据；这种程度的疲劳对判断力、药物计算和反应时间的损害与酒精相当。让搭档开车改变不了你的临床决策；兴奋剂只能掩盖困意，恢复不了表现；「先干着看看」等于拿最初几位患者做测试。向主管报告才是专业的做法——职业道德准则把患者福祉置于一切之上，各机构制定疲劳管理政策，正是为了让队员可以无责停勤。

questions.questionEn: Why is pulling an all-nighter before a skills examination counterproductive?
questions.questionZh: 为什么技能考试前通宵不睡会适得其反？

options.en: Caffeine taken after midnight blocks the consolidation of long-term memory
options.zh: 午夜后摄入的咖啡因会阻断长期记忆的巩固

options.en: At 17–19 hours awake, performance matches a blood alcohol of about 0.05%
options.zh: 连续清醒 17–19 小时后，表现相当于血液酒精浓度约 0.05%

options.en: Sleep does not affect memory, but examiners deduct marks for visible tiredness
options.zh: 睡眠不影响记忆，只是考官会因为你看起来疲惫而扣分

options.en: Late-night study improves retention as long as you stay well hydrated
options.zh: 只要补足水分，熬夜学习反而能提高记忆保持

questions.explanationEn: Dawson and Reid's classic study found that after about 17 hours awake, performance on cognitive and motor tasks matches a blood-alcohol level of 0.05%, and after 24 hours about 0.10% — well past legal driving limits. Sleep is also when the hippocampus consolidates what you practised during the day, so skipping it weakens exactly the memories the exam will test. Spaced review across the week with a full night's sleep before the exam is the evidence-based approach. Caffeine does not erase memories (it just disrupts the sleep you need), and examiners score your performance, not your appearance.
questions.explanationZh: Dawson 和 Reid 的经典研究发现：连续清醒约 17 小时后，认知和运动任务的表现相当于血液酒精浓度 0.05%，24 小时后约相当于 0.10%——远超法定驾驶限值。睡眠也是海马体巩固白天练习内容的时段，跳过它削弱的恰恰是考试要考的那些记忆。一周内分散复习、考前睡足一整晚，才是有证据支持的做法。咖啡因不会抹掉记忆（它只是搅乱你需要的睡眠）；考官打分看的是你的表现，不是气色。

questions.questionEn: It is 03:30 on your fourth consecutive night shift and you have about 45 minutes with no calls pending. Which fatigue countermeasure has the best support?
questions.questionZh: 你连上第四个夜班，凌晨 3:30，眼下大约有 45 分钟没有待处理的呼叫。哪种抗疲劳措施最有依据？

options.en: A 90-minute nap in the crew room, so that you complete one full sleep cycle before dawn
options.zh: 在休息室睡 90 分钟，天亮前睡满一个完整睡眠周期

options.en: Two energy drinks and some bright phone-screen time to stay alert
options.zh: 两罐能量饮料加刷一会儿亮屏手机提神

options.en: A 20-minute nap, caffeine just before it, and no caffeine late in the shift
options.zh: 小睡 20 分钟，躺下前喝咖啡因，后半班不再碰咖啡因

options.en: No food for the rest of the shift, to avoid a post-meal slump
options.zh: 后半班不吃东西，避免饭后犯困

questions.explanationEn: Brief naps of 10–20 minutes restore alertness without the heavy grogginess (sleep inertia) that follows waking from deep sleep — the likely result of a 90-minute nap that a call interrupts at the wrong moment. Caffeine takes about 20–30 minutes to act, so taking it immediately before a short nap means you wake as it kicks in; taking it late in the shift sabotages the daytime sleep you need to recover. Bright screens and sugar give a brief lift followed by a crash. Light, regular food is better than fasting. Cumulative sleep debt over consecutive nights is the real risk, so planning recovery sleep matters as much as any in-shift tactic.
questions.explanationZh: 10–20 分钟的小睡能恢复警觉，又不会出现从深睡中醒来时那种沉重的迷糊感（睡眠惰性）——睡 90 分钟而被呼叫在最糟的时刻叫醒，多半就是这个结果。咖啡因大约 20–30 分钟起效，所以在小睡前立刻喝，醒来时正好起作用；下班前几小时再喝，则会毁掉你恢复所需的白天睡眠。亮屏和糖分只能短暂提神，随后就是低谷。少量规律进食比饿着好。连续夜班累积的睡眠债才是真正的风险，所以安排恢复性睡眠和任何班中对策同样重要。

questions.questionEn: A normally talkative partner has gone quiet over the past month, cancelled the crew's social plans twice, and now vapes constantly between calls. After a hard paediatric call last week he said, 'I'm fine — drop it.' What is the best next step?
questions.questionZh: 搭档平时很健谈，这一个月却变得沉默，两次取消了车组的聚会，现在出诊间隙不停地抽电子烟。上周一次棘手的儿科出诊后他说：「我没事——别提了。」最好的下一步是什么？

options.en: Speak privately, describe what you've noticed, listen, and offer peer support
options.zh: 私下谈，说出你观察到的变化，倾听，并提供同伴支持的联系

options.en: Take 'I'm fine' at face value and wait until he chooses to raise it himself
options.zh: 相信「我没事」，等他自己愿意开口再说

options.en: Report him to the supervisor straight away as unfit for work
options.zh: 直接向主管报告他不适合上岗

options.en: Arrange a surprise group intervention with the whole crew at the station after shift
options.zh: 下班后在站里组织全车组出其不意的集体劝谈

questions.explanationEn: A change from someone's baseline — withdrawal, dropping social contact, new or increased substance use — is the early warning that matters, and 'I'm fine' is often what people say when they do not yet have words for what is happening. A private, specific, non-judgemental conversation keeps the door open; offering a concrete route (BCEHS runs a critical-incident stress management and peer-support program, and employee assistance counselling is available) makes help easy to accept. Waiting indefinitely abandons him; going to the supervisor first, with no performance or safety concern, breaks trust and may be the only thing he remembers; a group ambush humiliates. The exception is risk: any hint of suicidal thinking is handled immediately — stay with him, involve the service, and Canada's 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline is available by call or text.
questions.explanationZh: 偏离一个人平时基线的变化——退缩、放弃社交、新出现或加重的物质使用——才是真正要紧的早期信号，而「我没事」常常是人还没找到词来描述自己状况时的说法。私下、具体、不评判的交谈能把门留着；给出一条具体的路径（BCEHS 有危机事件压力管理和同伴支持项目，员工援助计划也提供咨询）会让接受帮助变得容易。无限期等待等于把他丢下；在没有任何表现或安全问题的情况下先找主管，会破坏信任，而且可能成为他唯一记住的事；集体「突袭」只会让人难堪。唯一的例外是风险：一旦有任何自杀念头的迹象，就要立刻处理——陪着他、让机构介入，加拿大的 9-8-8 自杀危机热线可以拨打或发短信。

questions.questionEn: What most clearly distinguishes a Critical Incident Stress Management (CISM) debriefing from an operational debrief held after a call?
questions.questionZh: 危机事件压力管理（CISM）复盘和出诊后的业务复盘（operational debrief），最明显的区别是什么？

options.en: CISM is mandatory after every cardiac arrest; operational debriefs are optional
options.zh: 每次心脏骤停后 CISM 都是强制的；业务复盘是可选的

options.en: Operational debriefs are led by a psychologist; CISM is run by the attending crew
options.zh: 业务复盘由心理学家主持；CISM 由出诊车组自己进行

options.en: Operational debriefs review performance; CISM helps people process reactions
options.zh: 业务复盘回顾表现；CISM 帮助人们消化自己的反应

options.en: They are the same meeting, held under two different names in different services
options.zh: 两者是同一场会议，只是不同机构叫法不同

questions.explanationEn: An operational debrief asks 'what happened, what went well, what would we change?' — it is about performance and systems and is appropriate after any significant call, including a routine resuscitation that went as expected. A CISM intervention is reserved for critical incidents — the death of a child, a colleague seriously hurt, violence against the crew, a mass-casualty event — and follows a structured sequence (in the Mitchell model: introduction, fact, thought, reaction, symptom, teaching and re-entry phases), usually a defusing within hours and a debriefing one to three days later. It is confidential, never compulsory, and is not a review of anyone's clinical decisions. Mixing the two — critiquing performance in a CISM session, or expecting an operational huddle to do emotional processing — undermines both.
questions.explanationZh: 业务复盘问的是「发生了什么、哪些做得好、下次改什么」——关注的是表现和系统，任何重要出诊之后都适用，包括一次结局符合预期的常规复苏。CISM 干预则专门针对危机事件——儿童死亡、同事重伤、车组遭受暴力、大规模伤亡事件——并按结构化顺序进行（Mitchell 模型分为引入、事实、想法、反应、症状、教育和回归七个阶段），通常是数小时内先做一次缓解谈话（defusing），一到三天后再做复盘。它是保密的、从不强制，也不审查任何人的临床决策。把两者混在一起——在 CISM 里批评表现，或者指望业务碰头会来处理情绪——两边都会被削弱。

questions.questionEn: Three years into the job, a colleague says she dreads every shift, feels nothing when patients thank her, refers to regular callers as 'the drunks', and believes nothing she does makes any difference. She has no flashbacks or nightmares. What does this pattern most suggest?
questions.questionZh: 入行三年的一位同事说，她害怕每一个班，患者道谢时毫无感觉，把常打电话的人叫作「那帮酒鬼」，觉得自己做什么都没有意义。她没有闪回，也没有噩梦。这种表现最符合什么？

options.en: An acute stress reaction to a single critical incident she has not disclosed
options.zh: 对某一次她没有说出来的危机事件的急性应激反应

options.en: Post-traumatic stress disorder with predominantly avoidant features
options.zh: 以回避为主要特征的创伤后应激障碍

options.en: Normal adaptation to years of rotating shift work and night duty
options.zh: 对多年轮班和夜班的正常适应

options.en: Burnout — exhaustion, depersonalisation and a reduced sense of personal accomplishment
options.zh: 职业倦怠——耗竭、去人格化和个人成就感降低

questions.explanationEn: The three classic dimensions of burnout are all here: emotional exhaustion (dreading shifts, feeling nothing), depersonalisation or cynicism toward the people served ('the drunks'), and a collapsed sense of personal accomplishment. Burnout builds gradually from chronic organisational and operational stressors — workload, offload delays, lack of control — rather than from one event. PTSD, by contrast, follows a potentially psychologically traumatic event and features intrusion (flashbacks, nightmares), avoidance and hyperarousal; an acute stress reaction is the short-lived response in the days after such an event. Cynicism toward patients is also a patient-safety signal, because it feeds diagnostic shortcuts. The useful response is early: a conversation, peer support or counselling, and attention to the workload drivers.
questions.explanationZh: 职业倦怠的三个经典维度都在：情绪耗竭（害怕上班、毫无感觉）、对服务对象的去人格化或玩世不恭（「那帮酒鬼」），以及个人成就感的崩塌。倦怠是由长期的组织和业务压力——工作负荷、交接等待、缺乏掌控感——逐渐累积而成，而不是源自某一个事件。相比之下，PTSD 发生在潜在心理创伤事件之后，特征是闯入（闪回、噩梦）、回避和高唤醒；急性应激反应则是事件后几天内的短暂反应。对患者的冷嘲热讽同时也是患者安全信号，因为它会助长诊断上的走捷径。有用的应对要趁早：谈一谈、同伴支持或心理咨询，并关注造成负荷的根源。

questions.questionEn: Six weeks after a fatal collision involving a child, a paramedic still has nightmares several times a week, drives a long detour to avoid the intersection, startles at sirens, and has begun drinking three or four beers every night to get to sleep. He insists it will pass on its own. Which response is most appropriate?
questions.questionZh: 一起导致儿童死亡的车祸过去六周了，一名护理员仍然每周做好几次噩梦，宁愿绕远路也不经过那个路口，听到警笛就惊跳，并且开始每晚喝三四瓶啤酒才能入睡。他坚称会自己好起来。哪种回应最恰当？

options.en: Agree with him — most such reactions settle on their own within a few months without help
options.zh: 认同他——这类反应大多几个月内不用帮助也会自行消退

options.en: Encourage him to see a mental-health professional now, via EFAP or his physician
options.zh: 鼓励他现在就通过员工援助计划或家庭医生去看心理健康专业人员

options.en: Suggest he replace the beer with a prescribed sleeping pill for a few weeks
options.zh: 建议他把啤酒换成处方安眠药吃几周

options.en: Tell him to drive through the intersection daily until it stops bothering him
options.zh: 让他每天开车经过那个路口，直到不再难受为止

questions.explanationEn: A stress reaction in the first days or weeks after a traumatic call is expected. What changes the picture here is duration and pattern: re-experiencing, avoidance and hyperarousal persisting past a month are the core features of post-traumatic stress disorder and need assessment and treatment, which works best when started early. Nightly alcohol to induce sleep is a coping pattern that fragments sleep, deepens low mood and raises risk — swapping it for a sedative only changes the crutch. Self-directed 'exposure' without a therapist's structure can retraumatise rather than desensitise. Untreated symptoms also erode judgement and reaction time, so this is a fitness-to-practise issue as well as a personal one. If he ever voices thoughts of ending his life, do not leave him alone, involve the service, and use Canada's 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline.
questions.explanationZh: 创伤性出诊后最初几天到几周内出现应激反应是可以预期的。这里改变判断的是持续时间和模式：再体验、回避和高唤醒持续超过一个月，正是创伤后应激障碍的核心特征，需要评估和治疗，而且越早开始效果越好。每晚靠酒精入睡会打碎睡眠结构、加重低落情绪、提高风险——换成镇静剂只是换了一根拐杖。没有治疗师框架的自行「暴露」可能造成再次创伤而不是脱敏。未经治疗的症状还会侵蚀判断力和反应速度，所以这既是个人问题，也是执业适格问题。如果他说出过结束生命的念头，不要让他独处，让机构介入，并使用加拿大的 9-8-8 自杀危机热线。

questions.questionEn: Which personal resilience goal is written in SMART form?
questions.questionZh: 下列哪个个人韧性目标是按 SMART 原则写的？

options.en: 'For eight weeks I'll run 30 minutes before three day shifts a week and log each run.'
options.zh: 「接下来八周，我每周在三个白班前跑步 30 分钟，每次都记录。」

options.en: 'Over the coming months I will get a lot fitter overall and handle my stress much better.'
options.zh: 「接下来几个月，我要整体上变得更健康，也更会应对压力。」

options.en: 'From now on I will never again let a bad call get to me or affect my home life.'
options.zh: 「从现在起，我再也不会让糟糕的出诊影响到我或我的家庭生活。」

options.en: 'I will meditate whenever I remember to, especially after the harder shifts.'
options.zh: 「想起来的时候我就冥想，特别是比较难熬的班之后。」

questions.explanationEn: A SMART goal is Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. The running goal names the behaviour, the amount, the frequency, the method of tracking and the end date, so you can tell on any given week whether you are on track. 'Fitter and handle stress better' cannot be measured; 'never let a call get to me' is both unachievable and a suppression goal, which works against resilience; and 'whenever I remember' has no schedule, so it will quietly disappear under shift work.
questions.explanationZh: SMART 目标要具体（Specific）、可衡量（Measurable）、可达成（Achievable）、相关（Relevant）、有时限（Time-bound）。跑步那条写明了行为、量、频率、记录方式和截止日期，任何一周都能判断自己有没有做到。「更健康、更会应对压力」无法衡量；「再也不让出诊影响到我」既做不到，又是一个压抑式的目标，与韧性背道而驰；「想起来就做」没有任何安排，在轮班生活里会悄无声息地消失。

questions.questionEn: Under BC's Emergency Health Services Act, on which of the following grounds may the Licensing Board — after a hearing — impose conditions on, suspend or revoke an EMA's licence?
questions.questionZh: 依据 BC《Emergency Health Services Act》，发牌委员会经听证后，可以基于下列哪一项对 EMA 的执照附加条件、暂停或吊销？

options.en: Declining voluntary overtime during a prolonged staffing shortage
options.zh: 长期人手短缺期间拒绝自愿加班

options.en: Falling two credits short of the annual continuing-education target on one occasion
options.zh: 某一年继续教育学分比年度要求少了两个

options.en: A single complaint about an abrupt manner, before any investigation
options.zh: 任何调查之前收到的一宗关于态度生硬的投诉

options.en: An addiction or ailment that materially impairs the ability to act as an EMA
options.zh: 严重影响履行 EMA 职责能力的成瘾或疾病

questions.explanationEn: Section 7 of the Act lets the Board, after a hearing, find that an EMA has carried out duties incompetently, has breached a licence condition, or suffers from a physical ailment, emotional disturbance or addiction that materially impairs their ability to practise — and then impose conditions, suspend, revoke, or bar the person from licensure for a period. That is the legal meaning of 'fitness to practise': health matters when it impairs the work, and the protective path is to seek treatment early and be honest with your employer rather than hide it. A complaint only starts an investigation; it is not itself a finding. A continuing-education shortfall is handled first through the director's process in the Regulation (notice, a chance to respond, possibly an evaluating examination), not by discipline for a single gap. Refusing overtime is an employment matter, not a licensing one.
questions.explanationZh: 该法第 7 条规定，Board 经听证后可以认定某 EMA 不胜任地履行职责、违反执照条件，或患有严重影响其执业能力的身体疾病、情绪障碍或成瘾——进而附加条件、暂停、吊销执照，或在一定期限内禁止其持牌。这就是「执业适格」在法律上的含义：健康问题只有在影响工作时才成为问题，而保护自己的路径是及早治疗、对雇主坦诚，而不是隐瞒。一宗投诉只是启动调查，本身不是结论。继续教育学分不足首先走法规中 director 的程序（通知、申辩机会、可能的评估考试），不会因为一次差距就直接受纪律处分。拒绝加班是劳动关系问题，与执照无关。

questions.questionEn: In an SBAR radio report, which statement belongs under 'Recommendation'?
questions.questionZh: 在 SBAR 无线电报告中，下列哪句话属于「R——建议（Recommendation）」部分？

options.en: '68-year-old man, crushing chest pain for the last 40 minutes.'
options.zh: 「68 岁男性，压榨性胸痛 40 分钟。」

options.en: 'Requesting STEMI pathway activation and a resuscitation bed; ETA 12 minutes.'
options.zh: 「请启动 STEMI 通道并准备抢救床；预计 12 分钟到达。」

options.en: 'History of hypertension and a coronary stent in 2019; takes ramipril daily.'
options.zh: 「高血压病史，2019 年置入冠脉支架；每日服用雷米普利。」

options.en: '12-lead shows ST elevation in V2 to V4; I believe this is an anterior wall STEMI.'
options.zh: 「12 导联 V2–V4 ST 段抬高；我判断是前壁 STEMI。」

questions.explanationEn: SBAR orders a report so the listener hears what they need in a predictable sequence: Situation (who the patient is and the problem in one line), Background (the relevant history and medications), Assessment (what you think is happening, with the key findings that support it) and Recommendation (what you are asking the receiving team to do or prepare). The request for pathway activation and a bed is the Recommendation. The one-line description of the man and his pain is the Situation, the stent and ramipril are Background, and the ECG interpretation is your Assessment.
questions.explanationZh: SBAR 把报告排成可预期的顺序，让听的人按需接收信息：S 情况（患者是谁、问题是什么，一句话）、B 背景（相关病史和用药）、A 评估（你判断发生了什么，以及支持判断的关键发现）、R 建议（你请接收团队做什么或准备什么）。请求启动通道并准备床位就是「建议」。一句话描述患者和胸痛是「情况」，支架和雷米普利是「背景」，心电图解读是你的「评估」。

questions.questionEn: Your pre-alert for a pedestrian struck at about 40 km/h runs: 'M — pedestrian hit by a car, thrown roughly 3 metres. I — deformed left thigh, abrasions to the left arm, no head injury found. S — HR 118, BP 100/70, RR 22, SpO₂ 97%, GCS 15.' Which MIST element has been left out?
questions.questionZh: 你对一名被时速约 40 km/h 汽车撞倒的行人发出预警：「M——行人被汽车撞击，抛出约 3 米。I——左大腿畸形，左臂擦伤，未发现头部损伤。S——HR 118，BP 100/70，RR 22，SpO₂ 97%，GCS 15。」MIST 里漏掉了哪一项？

options.en: Mechanism — the report should state the vehicle type and point of impact
options.zh: 受伤机制——报告应说明车型和撞击部位

options.en: Injuries — the report should list suspected pelvic and spinal injuries too
options.zh: 损伤——报告还应列出可疑的骨盆和脊柱损伤

options.en: Signs — the report should include a pain score and skin findings
options.zh: 体征——报告应包含疼痛评分和皮肤表现

options.en: Treatment — what has been done so far and how the patient responded
options.zh: 处置——到目前为止做了什么、患者反应如何

questions.explanationEn: MIST is the trauma pre-alert structure: Mechanism, Injuries found or suspected, Signs (vital signs and level of consciousness) and Treatment given. The report covers the first three well — the mechanism includes the speed and distance thrown, the injuries are listed by region, and the signs include a full set of vitals — but says nothing about what has been done. The receiving trauma team needs to know whether a traction splint is on, whether TXA or fluids have been started and when, and whether the tachycardia has changed with treatment; otherwise they may duplicate or delay care.
questions.explanationZh: MIST 是创伤预警的结构：受伤机制（Mechanism）、已发现或怀疑的损伤（Injuries）、体征（Signs，包括生命体征和意识水平）、已给予的处置（Treatment）。这份报告前三项都不错——机制写了车速和抛出距离，损伤按部位列出，体征有完整一组——却完全没说做了什么。接收的创伤团队需要知道是否上了牵引夹板、TXA 或补液是否已经开始、何时开始、心动过速在处置后有没有变化；否则他们可能重复或延误处置。

questions.questionEn: According to the EMALB practical-examination grading criteria, which items are expected in the verbal hand-off report at the hospital but are not listed as required content of the earlier pre-arrival notification?
questions.questionZh: 按 EMALB 实操考试评分标准，下列哪些内容是到院口头交接必须包含、而此前的到院前通报（notification）并未列为必需的？

options.en: Medical history, medications, allergies, and final as well as initial vitals
options.zh: 既往史、用药、过敏史，以及最后一组和最初一组生命体征

options.en: The patient's age and gender, together with the unit's estimated time of arrival
options.zh: 患者的年龄和性别，以及车组预计到达时间

options.en: The chief complaint and the mechanism of injury, where there is one
options.zh: 主诉，以及（如有）受伤机制

options.en: The treatments and protocols given, and the patient's response to them
options.zh: 已给予的处置和流程，以及患者的反应

questions.explanationEn: The grading guide describes the pre-arrival notification as a short message so the hospital can prepare: age and gender, chief complaint, mechanism of injury if relevant, history of the chief complaint, vital signs, treatments or protocols given, and relevant physical findings. The verbal hand-off at the bedside is the full transfer of care, so the guide adds the patient's medical history, medications and allergies, and asks for both the initial and the final set of vital signs so the receiving team can see the trend. Failing to provide critical information in either report is graded as a moderate deficiency; failing to notify the hospital at all for a critical patient draws the heaviest deduction in the notification component.
questions.explanationZh: 评分指南把到院前通报定位为一条让医院做准备的简短信息：年龄和性别、主诉、相关时的受伤机制、现病史、生命体征、已给予的处置或流程，以及相关的体格检查发现。床旁口头交接是完整的照护转移，所以指南加上了患者的既往史、用药和过敏史，并要求同时报告最初和最后一组生命体征，让接收团队看到趋势。在任一报告中遗漏关键信息按中度缺陷扣分；对危重患者完全没有通报医院，是通报这一项里扣分最重的情形。

questions.questionEn: Which medication statement in a hand-off report gives the receiving team enough to decide safely about further bronchodilator?
questions.questionZh: 交接报告中的哪一句用药描述，足以让接收团队安全地决定是否继续给支气管扩张剂？

options.en: 'She had some Ventolin on the way in and seems a fair bit better than she was.'
options.zh: 「路上给了点 Ventolin，看起来比刚才好了不少。」

options.en: 'Salbutamol given en route as per the asthma protocol; patient improved, no adverse effects noted.'
options.zh: 「途中按哮喘流程给了沙丁胺醇；患者有改善，未见不良反应。」

options.en: 'Salbutamol 5 mg neb at 09:42 and 09:58; SpO₂ 91 to 95%, now speaking full sentences.'
options.zh: 「沙丁胺醇 5 mg 雾化，09:42 和 09:58 各一次；SpO₂ 从 91% 到 95%，现在能说完整句子。」

options.en: 'Two nebs given, no problems; she says she feels much better than before we arrived.'
options.zh: 「做了两次雾化，没问题；她说比我们到之前舒服多了。」

questions.explanationEn: A medication handover is complete when the listener could reconstruct exactly what happened: the drug, the dose, the route, the time of each administration and the measurable response. The complete statement lets the ED calculate when the next dose is due, judge whether the response is adequate and recognise that two doses have already been given. 'Some Ventolin' and 'patient improved' leave the dose, timing and the size of the improvement to guesswork, and 'no problems' describes neither the drug nor its effect. This mirrors the AET course's five elements for handing over a drug and the 'right documentation' expectation on the EMALB practical exam, where drug timings must reflect the time of original administration.
questions.explanationZh: 用药交接的完成标准是：听的人能够完整还原发生过什么——哪种药、多少量、什么途径、每一次给药的时间，以及可测量的反应。那句完整的描述让急诊能算出下一剂该什么时候给、判断反应是否充分、并知道已经用过两剂。「给了点 Ventolin」和「有改善」把剂量、时间和改善幅度都留给猜测；「没问题」既没说药也没说效果。这正对应 AET 课上讲的用药交接五要素，以及 EMALB 实操考试对「正确记录」的要求——给药时间必须以首次给药时刻为准。

questions.questionEn: You begin your hand-off to an emergency physician who immediately starts his own examination and talks to the patient over you, before you have reached the allergies or the medication times. What is the best way to handle this?
questions.questionZh: 你刚开始向急诊医生交接，他立刻自己查起体来，隔着你和患者说话，而你还没讲到过敏史和给药时间。最好的处理方式是什么？

options.en: Stop talking, write the rest on the PCR, and leave as soon as he has taken the patient
options.zh: 不说了，剩下的写进 PCR，他一接手患者就离开

options.en: Pause him politely, state that 60 seconds of critical items remain, and finish
options.zh: 礼貌地打断他，说明还有 60 秒的关键内容，然后讲完

options.en: Raise your voice and restart the whole report from the beginning
options.zh: 提高嗓门，从头把整份报告再讲一遍

options.en: Give the remaining information to the unit clerk at the desk instead
options.zh: 把剩下的信息改告诉前台的病区文员

questions.explanationEn: Handover is a two-way transfer of responsibility, and critical items such as allergies and medication times only protect the patient if the clinician taking over actually hears them. A brief, respectful, assertive statement that names why the information matters and promises to take questions afterwards is the professional way to regain attention — the 'no interruptions during handover' principle that high-reliability teams use. Writing it on the PCR alone is not a handover, and a verbal report with critical information missing is graded as a moderate deficiency on the practical exam. Shouting damages the relationship and wastes time, and the clerk is not a clinician who can act on the information.
questions.explanationZh: 交接是责任的双向转移，过敏史、给药时间这类关键信息，只有在真正接手的医护听到之后才能保护患者。一句简短、有礼、坚定的话——说明这些信息为什么重要、并承诺讲完就回答问题——是重新获得注意力的专业方式，也就是高可靠性团队奉行的「交接中不打断」原则。只写进 PCR 不算交接；口头报告缺了关键信息，在实操考试中按中度缺陷扣分。提高嗓门会伤害关系、浪费时间；文员不是能依据这些信息采取行动的医护。

questions.questionEn: Which patient most needs an early pre-arrival notification to the receiving hospital?
questions.questionZh: 下列哪位患者最需要尽早向接收医院发出到院前通报？

options.en: A 24-year-old with a twisted ankle, normal vital signs, 5 minutes from hospital
options.zh: 24 岁扭伤脚踝，生命体征正常，距医院 5 分钟

options.en: A 50-year-old whose indigestion-like pain has resolved, with a normal 12-lead
options.zh: 50 岁，消化不良样不适已缓解，12 导联正常

options.en: A 30-year-old with a small laceration that will need suturing in the ED
options.zh: 30 岁，小裂伤需要到急诊缝合

options.en: A 72-year-old with new facial droop and arm weakness, last seen well 50 minutes ago
options.zh: 72 岁，新发面瘫和上肢无力，最后一次被看到正常是 50 分钟前

questions.explanationEn: Pre-arrival notification exists so the hospital can have the right people and resources ready the moment the patient arrives. That matters most when treatment is time-critical: an acute stroke patient within the treatment window needs the CT scanner cleared and the stroke team assembled, and the BC guidelines for stroke specifically call for timely transport with notification of the receiving facility en route. The other three patients still receive a report, but nothing is lost by giving it on arrival. Under the exam grading criteria, failing to notify at all for a critical patient is the heaviest notification deduction, and a delay in notifying for a critical patient is a moderate one — while failing to notify for a non-critical patient is also marked, so every patient gets some form of notification.
questions.explanationZh: 到院前通报的意义在于让医院在患者到达的那一刻就备好人员和资源。治疗有时间窗时这最关键：在治疗窗内的急性卒中患者需要腾出 CT、集结卒中团队，BC 考纲的卒中部分也明确要求及时转运并在途中通知接收医院。另外三位患者同样要有报告，但到达后再说也不会损失什么。按考试评分标准，对危重患者完全不通报是通报项里扣分最重的；对危重患者延迟通报属中度缺陷；对非危重患者不通报也会被扣分——所以每位患者都要以某种形式通报。

questions.questionEn: After treating a man for a dangerously slow heart rhythm you need to explain the situation to his anxious wife, and then hand over to the ED nurse. Which pairing is right?
questions.questionZh: 你处理了一名心率过慢的男性患者，现在要向他焦急的妻子解释情况，随后向急诊护士交接。哪种搭配是对的？

options.en: Plain words for the wife; precise clinical terms and numbers for the nurse
options.zh: 对妻子用大白话；对护士用精确的临床术语和数字

options.en: Clinical wording for both — accuracy means the same thing for everyone
options.zh: 对两人都用临床术语——准确性对谁都一样

options.en: Plain language for both — technical terms only ever cause confusion
options.zh: 对两人都用大白话——术语只会造成混乱

options.en: Give the wife the full rhythm diagnosis first so she can pass it to the nurse
options.zh: 先把完整的心律诊断告诉妻子，让她转告护士

questions.explanationEn: Match the language to the listener. Family members need plain words that convey what is wrong and what happens next without inducing panic or false reassurance; most adults struggle with medical terminology, and a frightened spouse hears even less. Clinicians need precise terminology because it is faster and unambiguous — 'third-degree block at 34' tells the nurse in five words what to prepare for. Using jargon with the family fails them; using only plain language with the nurse loses precision and wastes time. A relative must never be the channel for a clinical handover: information degrades, and the responsibility to report is yours.
questions.explanationZh: 语言要配合听的人。家属需要的是大白话——讲清出了什么事、接下来会怎样，既不引起恐慌也不给虚假的安慰；大多数成年人本就听不懂医学术语，惊慌的配偶听进去的更少。医护则需要精确的术语，因为它更快、不含糊——「三度阻滞、心率 34」五个词就告诉护士该准备什么。对家属用术语是辜负他们；对护士只用大白话则丢掉精度、浪费时间。亲属绝不能成为临床交接的中转：信息会在传递中失真，而报告的责任在你。

questions.questionEn: A man found apneic after a suspected fentanyl overdose was ventilated with a bag-valve-mask for four minutes and then given naloxone; he is now breathing on his own. In your hand-off you report the naloxone dose and time but never mention that he was apneic and ventilated. Why does this omission matter?
questions.questionZh: 一名疑似芬太尼过量的男性被发现时呼吸停止，先用 BVM 通气了四分钟，再给了纳洛酮；现在他已能自主呼吸。你交接时报告了纳洛酮的剂量和时间，却没有提到他曾呼吸停止、被人工通气。为什么这个遗漏很要紧？

options.en: It does not matter — he is breathing normally now, so it is history
options.zh: 不要紧——他现在呼吸正常，那已经是过去的事

options.en: It matters only for billing codes and the service's statistics
options.zh: 只对计费编码和机构统计有影响

options.en: It is critical information the receiving team needs for its monitoring plan
options.zh: 这是接收团队制定监测计划所需的关键信息

options.en: It matters only if the family later asks about what happened before the hospital
options.zh: 只有家属事后问起到院前发生了什么时才要紧

questions.explanationEn: A period of apnea tells the receiving team how severe the overdose was and how hard he may fall again when the naloxone wears off — its effect lasts roughly 30 to 90 minutes, shorter than many opioids. Positive-pressure ventilation of an unprotected airway also raises the chance of gastric insufflation and aspiration. Without that history the ED may under-monitor him or accept an early request to leave. The EMALB grading criteria list 'not reporting ventilating the apneic patient' as their own example of failing to provide critical information potentially detrimental to patient care — a moderate deficiency in the notification and hand-off components. The ventilation also belongs on the PCR with its start and stop times.
questions.explanationZh: 曾经呼吸停止这一点，告诉接收团队这次过量有多严重、纳洛酮失效后他可能再次跌得多深——纳洛酮作用大约维持 30 到 90 分钟，比许多阿片类药物短。对未保护气道做正压通气还会增加胃胀气和误吸的风险。少了这段病史，急诊可能监测不足，或者轻易同意他早早离开。EMALB 评分标准把「未报告曾为呼吸停止患者通气」直接列为「遗漏可能危及患者照护的关键信息」的例子——在通报和交接两项中都属中度缺陷。通气及其起止时间同样要写进 PCR。

questions.questionEn: You tell your partner, 'Set up the nebuliser with salbutamol 5 mg.' Which reply completes closed-loop communication?
questions.questionZh: 你对搭档说：「准备雾化器，沙丁胺醇 5 mg。」哪种回应构成完整的闭环沟通？

options.en: A thumbs-up while he carries on with what he was already doing
options.zh: 他一边继续手头的事一边竖个大拇指

options.en: 'Nebuliser, salbutamol 5 mg — on it,' then 'Neb running' when done
options.zh: 「雾化器，沙丁胺醇 5 mg——这就弄」，做完再说「雾化已开始」

options.en: 'Okay,' followed by setting up the equipment without further comment
options.zh: 「好」，然后一声不吭地去准备设备

options.en: No reply is needed — he knows the protocol and the dose as well as you do
options.zh: 不用回应——流程和剂量他和你一样清楚

questions.explanationEn: Closed-loop communication has three parts: the sender gives a clear, directed instruction; the receiver repeats back the key content so any mishearing (wrong drug, wrong dose) is caught before it happens; and the sender confirms, with a completion report closing the loop when the task is done. 'Okay', a gesture or silence confirm that something was heard, not what. On the practical exam, communication with your partner is assessed under overall call management, and the same read-back habit protects your hospital handover when you ask the receiver to repeat the allergy or the medication times.
questions.explanationZh: 闭环沟通有三步：发出者给出清楚、有明确对象的指令；接收者复述关键内容，让听错（错药、错剂量）在发生之前被发现；发出者确认，任务完成后再以一句完成汇报把环闭上。「好」、手势或沉默只能证明听到了什么，不能证明听到的是什么。实操考试中，与搭档的沟通计入整体出诊管理；同样的复述习惯也保护你的医院交接——请接收者复述过敏史或给药时间。

questions.questionEn: In SBAR, which of the following is an example of the 'Assessment' component?
questions.questionZh: 在 SBAR 中，下列哪句属于「A——评估（Assessment）」部分？

options.en: 'This is Unit 23 with a 55-year-old woman, about 10 minutes out.'
options.zh: 「这里是 23 号车，一名 55 岁女性，约 10 分钟到。」

options.en: 'She has type 2 diabetes and was treated for a kidney infection last month.'
options.zh: 「她有 2 型糖尿病，上个月治疗过肾脏感染。」

options.en: 'Please have a bed ready and consider early antibiotics on arrival.'
options.zh: 「请备好床位，到达后考虑尽早使用抗生素。」

options.en: 'Temp 39.2, HR 124, BP 86/50, new confusion — I think she is septic.'
options.zh: 「体温 39.2，HR 124，BP 86/50，新发意识模糊——我判断是脓毒症。」

questions.explanationEn: Assessment is your clinical impression together with the findings that support it — here the fever, tachycardia, hypotension and new confusion leading to the conclusion of probable sepsis. The unit identification and the one-line description of the patient is the Situation; the diabetes and the recent infection are Background; asking for a bed and early antibiotics is the Recommendation. Keeping the impression in the Assessment slot, rather than scattering numbers through the report, is what lets the receiving team act on it quickly.
questions.explanationZh: 评估是你的临床印象加上支持它的发现——这里是发热、心动过速、低血压和新发意识模糊，得出很可能是脓毒症的结论。报车号和一句话介绍患者是「情况」；糖尿病和近期感染是「背景」；要求备床和尽早用抗生素是「建议」。把印象放在「评估」这一格，而不是把数字零散地撒在报告里，接收团队才能迅速据此行动。

questions.questionEn: Which pre-alert would most naturally be structured with MIST rather than SBAR?
questions.questionZh: 下列哪种预警最自然地适合用 MIST 而不是 SBAR 来组织？

options.en: A 19-year-old thrown from a motorcycle with an unstable pelvis and shock
options.zh: 19 岁，骑摩托车被甩出，骨盆不稳定，有休克

options.en: A 70-year-old with worsening shortness of breath and known heart failure
options.zh: 70 岁，呼吸困难加重，有心力衰竭病史

options.en: A 45-year-old with a severe allergic reaction after a bee sting at a picnic
options.zh: 45 岁，野餐时被蜜蜂蜇后严重过敏反应

options.en: A 60-year-old with sudden slurred speech and a new facial droop
options.zh: 60 岁，突发言语含糊和新发面瘫

questions.explanationEn: MIST — Mechanism, Injuries, Signs, Treatment — was built for trauma, where the mechanism itself predicts injuries the team should look for and the injury list drives the resources (blood, surgery, imaging) they prepare. SBAR is a general clinical structure that fits medical presentations such as heart failure, anaphylaxis and stroke, where history and clinical impression matter more than a mechanism. IMIST-AMBO extends MIST with identification, allergies, medications, background and other information for the bedside hand-off. The examiner grades whether the report is organised and complete, not which acronym you used — so pick the structure that carries the content best.
questions.explanationZh: MIST——机制、损伤、体征、处置——是为创伤设计的：机制本身就能预测团队该找哪些损伤，损伤清单决定他们要准备什么资源（血、手术、影像）。SBAR 是通用的临床结构，适合心衰、过敏反应、卒中这类内科表现，病史和临床印象比机制更重要。IMIST-AMBO 在 MIST 基础上加入身份、过敏、用药、背景和其他信息，用于床旁交接。考官评的是报告是否有条理、是否完整，而不是你用了哪个缩写——所以选最能承载内容的结构。

questions.questionEn: The emergency department is overflowing. The triage nurse waves toward a hallway spot and says, 'Just park him there, I'll get to him,' without hearing your report. Your 79-year-old patient has new atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular rate and is still on your monitor. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 急诊人满为患。分诊护士朝走廊的一个位置挥挥手：「先把他放那儿，我待会儿过去」，并没有听你报告。你这位 79 岁的患者新发房颤、心室率快，还连着你的监护仪。你该怎么做？

options.en: Leave him in the hallway with the PCR on his lap and clear for the next call
options.zh: 把他留在走廊，PCR 放在他腿上，然后出车接下一单

options.en: Hand the monitor leads to a porter, note the time, and leave
options.zh: 把监护导线交给勤杂工，记下时间就走

options.en: Stay, keep monitoring, and hand over only to a nurse or physician who accepts care
options.zh: 留下继续监护，只向接收照护的护士或医生做交接

options.en: Transport him to a different hospital without informing anyone
options.zh: 不告诉任何人，把他转去另一家医院

questions.explanationEn: Until a clinician accepts the patient, he is still yours: a monitored patient with a new fast arrhythmia left unattended in a hallway is abandonment, and the record on his lap is not a handover. Stay, continue observations, repeat vital signs, and escalate to the charge nurse or your supervisor if the wait becomes unsafe; document the times and who finally accepted. A porter cannot take clinical responsibility, and leaving for another hospital without communication abandons the patient in a different way. On the practical exam the hand-off report is itself a graded component — failing to give one is marked as a deficiency.
questions.explanationZh: 在有医护接收之前，患者仍然是你的：一名带监护、新发快速心律失常的患者被独自留在走廊就是遗弃，腿上的那份记录不算交接。留下来，继续观察，复测生命体征，等待变得不安全时升级到护士长或你的主管；记录时间和最终由谁接收。勤杂工不能承担临床责任；不打招呼就转去另一家医院是另一种形式的遗弃。实操考试中交接报告本身就是评分项——不做交接会被记为缺陷。

questions.questionEn: What most clearly distinguishes cultural humility from cultural competence?
questions.questionZh: 文化谦逊（cultural humility）和文化胜任力（cultural competence）最明显的区别是什么？

options.en: Humility is taught in a certificate course, whereas competence is learned on the job
options.zh: 谦逊靠证书课程来教，而胜任力靠上班时积累

options.en: Competence applies to Indigenous patients; humility applies to newcomers
options.zh: 胜任力针对原住民患者；谦逊针对新移民

options.en: Humility is lifelong self-reflection; competence implies a mastered body of facts
options.zh: 谦逊是终身的自我反思；胜任力暗示一套可以掌握的知识

options.en: The two terms describe the same concept and are used interchangeably
options.zh: 两个词描述同一个概念，可以互换使用

questions.explanationEn: The cultural-competence model implies an endpoint: learn enough about a group and you are qualified to care for its members. In practice that invites stereotypes ('people from this culture believe…') and ignores how much individuals within any group differ. Cultural humility, as Tervalon and Murray-García framed it, has three commitments: ongoing self-critique about your own assumptions, deliberate attention to the power imbalance inherent in a uniformed provider standing over a patient, and holding institutions accountable. It applies to every patient, not one population, and it is a stance rather than a credential — which is why the useful question is 'What should I know to care for you well?' rather than a memorised checklist.
questions.explanationZh: 文化胜任力模型隐含一个终点：对某个群体了解得够多，你就有资格照顾它的成员。实践中这会招来刻板印象（「这种文化的人都相信……」），并且忽略了任何群体内部个体之间的巨大差异。Tervalon 和 Murray-García 提出的文化谦逊有三项承诺：对自身假设持续自我批判；刻意关注穿制服的医护俯视患者时固有的权力不对等；以及要求机构承担责任。它适用于每一位患者，而不是某一类人群；它是一种姿态而不是一张证书——所以有用的问法是「我需要知道什么才能照顾好您？」，而不是背下来的清单。

questions.questionEn: You feel a call went well: you were polite, explained each step and followed protocol. A week later the family complains that they felt judged and talked down to throughout. Who determines whether the encounter was culturally safe?
questions.questionZh: 你觉得这次出诊很顺利：态度礼貌、每一步都解释了、流程也都照做了。一周后家属投诉，说全程感觉被评判、被居高临下地对待。这次接触是否「文化安全」，由谁来判定？

options.en: You, after reflecting honestly on whether protocol and policy were followed
options.zh: 你自己，诚实地回顾流程和政策有没有照做

options.en: The patient and family — cultural safety is defined by their experience of the care
options.zh: 患者和家属——文化安全由他们对照护的体验来定义

options.en: The service's diversity officer, through a retrospective chart audit
options.zh: 机构的多元化专员，通过回顾性病历审核

options.en: The receiving hospital's triage nurse, who saw how the handover went
options.zh: 接收医院的分诊护士，她看到了交接的过程

questions.explanationEn: Cultural safety is an outcome judged by the person on the receiving end: did they feel respected, heard and free from discrimination? Good intentions and procedural correctness are necessary but do not settle the question, because tone, body language, assumptions and the history a family brings into the room all shape their experience. BC's 'In Plain Sight' review adopted exactly this recipient-defined standard. The professional response to the complaint is therefore not to defend the protocol but to ask what the family experienced, reflect on it honestly and adjust — that reflection is the core practice of cultural humility.
questions.explanationZh: 文化安全是由接受照护的一方来评判的结果：他们是否感到被尊重、被倾听、没有受到歧视？良好的本意和程序上的正确是必要的，但不能决定答案，因为语气、肢体语言、预设立场，以及家属带进房间的历史记忆，都在塑造他们的体验。BC 的《In Plain Sight》审查报告采用的正是这个「由接受者定义」的标准。所以面对投诉，专业的反应不是为流程辩护，而是去了解家属经历了什么、诚实地反思并调整——这种反思正是文化谦逊的核心实践。

questions.questionEn: The 2020 British Columbia review titled 'In Plain Sight' is relevant to paramedics because it:
questions.questionZh: 2020 年 BC 省的《In Plain Sight》审查报告之所以与护理员相关，是因为它：

options.en: Documented widespread Indigenous-specific racism and stereotyping in BC health care
options.zh: 记录了 BC 医疗系统中普遍存在的针对原住民的种族主义和刻板印象

options.en: Set maximum ambulance response times for rural and remote communities
options.zh: 规定了乡村和偏远社区救护车的最长响应时间

options.en: Ruled that health providers may not ask patients about their ethnicity
options.zh: 裁定医疗人员不得询问患者的族裔

options.en: Concluded that Indigenous-specific racism in BC health care had largely been eliminated by 2020
options.zh: 得出结论：到 2020 年 BC 医疗系统中针对原住民的种族主义已基本消除

questions.explanationEn: The independent review led by Mary Ellen Turpel-Lafond collected thousands of accounts and found Indigenous-specific racism to be widespread: a large majority of Indigenous respondents reported discrimination, and recurring stereotypes — 'drunk', 'drug-seeking', 'non-compliant', 'bad parent' — were shown to produce missed diagnoses, undertreated pain, longer waits and avoidance of care altogether. Its recommendations include cultural-safety and anti-racism training for all health workers, which is why the topic sits in a paramedic curriculum.
