For a crew the practical lesson is concrete: an assumption of intoxication is a stereotype, and a stereotype applied in place of an assessment is a patient-safety failure as well as an ethical one.
questions.explanationZh: 由 Mary Ellen Turpel-Lafond 主持的这项独立审查收集了数千份陈述，发现针对原住民的种族主义普遍存在：绝大多数原住民受访者报告遭遇过歧视；反复出现的刻板印象——「醉鬼」「求药」「不配合」「不称职的父母」——被证明导致漏诊、疼痛处理不足、等候更久，乃至彻底回避就医。报告的建议包括对所有医疗从业者进行文化安全和反种族主义培训，这正是这个主题进入护理员课程的原因。对车组来说，实际教训很具体：预设患者醉酒是一种刻板印象，而用刻板印象代替评估，既是伦理失误，也是患者安全事故。

questions.questionEn: A bystander flags you down for an Indigenous man slumped on a bus bench with slurred speech. The bystander says, 'He's always drunk — he's here every day.' You cannot confirm any smell of alcohol, and he is drowsy. What should guide your next step?
questions.questionZh: 一名路人拦下你们：一位原住民男性瘫坐在公交长椅上，言语含糊。路人说：「他天天在这儿，总是醉醺醺的。」你闻不到确切的酒味，他有些嗜睡。接下来该以什么为准？

options.en: Accept the bystander's history, help him sit up, and clear the call
options.zh: 采信路人的说法，扶他坐好，结束这单

options.en: Transport him directly to the nearest sobering centre without any further assessment
options.zh: 不再做任何评估，直接送往最近的醒酒中心

options.en: Ask him to walk a straight line to confirm that he is intoxicated
options.zh: 让他走直线来确认是否醉酒

options.en: Treat it as undiagnosed: glucose, stroke screen, pupils, temperature, full exam
options.zh: 当作尚未查明：测血糖、卒中筛查、看瞳孔、量体温、完整检查

questions.explanationEn: Slurred speech and drowsiness are produced by hypoglycemia, stroke, head injury, hypothermia, sepsis, post-ictal states and overdose as readily as by alcohol — and a man who really does drink daily can also have any of them. Diagnostic overshadowing is the error of attributing new findings to a known or assumed label and stopping there; applied to an Indigenous patient on the strength of a stranger's remark, it is exactly the pattern the 'In Plain Sight' review documented. The bystander's comment is recorded as reported history, nothing more. Check the glucose first, run a stroke screen, examine pupils and skin, take a temperature and complete the assessment. A sobering centre is a disposition for a patient who has been assessed, not a substitute for assessing one.
questions.explanationZh: 言语含糊和嗜睡可以由低血糖、卒中、头部外伤、低体温、脓毒症、发作后状态和药物过量引起，和酒精一样常见——而一个确实天天喝酒的人同样可能患上其中任何一种。诊断遮蔽（diagnostic overshadowing）就是把新出现的表现归因于一个已知或预设的标签然后止步不前；凭陌生人一句话就把它套在一位原住民患者身上，正是《In Plain Sight》报告记录的那种模式。路人的说法只能作为「他人提供的病史」记录下来，仅此而已。先测血糖，做卒中筛查，检查瞳孔和皮肤，量体温，完成评估。醒酒中心是评估之后的去向选项，不能代替评估本身。

questions.questionEn: A stable Indigenous patient being transported from home holds a small cloth medicine bundle and asks that it stay with her and not be opened. Your partner wants to bag it with her belongings 'for infection control'. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一位病情稳定的原住民患者从家中转运时，手里握着一个小布包的药囊（medicine bundle），要求它留在身边、不要打开。搭档想「为了感染控制」把它和她的其他物品一起装袋。你该怎么做？

options.en: Keep it with her unopened, record it in your hand-off report, ask what else would help
options.zh: 让它留在她身边不打开，写进交接报告，并问她还有什么能帮到她

options.en: Insist on bagging it, because all patient property is handled the same way
options.zh: 坚持装袋，因为所有患者物品都是同一处理方式

options.en: Open it to check for medications that could interact with your treatment
options.zh: 打开检查有没有会与治疗相互作用的药物

options.en: Ask her to leave it at home so that it is not lost during the hospital admission
options.zh: 让她把它留在家里，免得住院期间弄丢

questions.explanationEn: A medicine bundle is a sacred object, and in many Indigenous traditions it should not be opened or handled by others. Nothing about a small cloth bundle held in a stable patient's hands creates an infection-control problem, so the 'same for everyone' rule is being invoked to override a cultural need rather than to protect anyone. Opening it to look for medications confuses a sacred item with a pill bottle — medication history is obtained by asking. Keeping it with her, recording it in the hand-off so the next team does not remove it, and asking what else matters to her are the practical expressions of cultural safety; the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's Call to Action 22 asks the health system to recognise and make room for Indigenous healing practices where patients request them.
questions.explanationZh: 药囊是神圣物品，在许多原住民传统里不应由他人打开或触碰。病情稳定的患者手里握着一个小布包，不构成任何感染控制问题，所以「人人一样」在这里是在用规则压过文化需求，而不是在保护谁。为了找药而打开它，是把圣物当成了药瓶——用药史靠询问获得。让它留在她身边、在交接中记录下来以免下一组人把它拿走、再问她还有什么重要的事，这些都是文化安全的具体做法；真相与和解委员会第 22 号行动呼吁，要求医疗系统在患者提出时承认并为原住民的疗愈实践留出空间。

questions.questionEn: Which statement best describes intersectionality as it applies to patient care?
questions.questionZh: 下列哪项最准确地描述了「交叉性」（intersectionality）在患者照护中的含义？

options.en: Every patient should be treated identically regardless of their background
options.zh: 不论背景，每位患者都应得到完全相同的对待

options.en: Overlapping identities combine into a distinct, compounded experience of barriers
options.zh: 多重身份叠加成一种独特的、复合的障碍经历

options.en: Patients with several marginalised identities should be referred to a specialist clinic
options.zh: 有多重边缘身份的患者应转诊到专科门诊

options.en: Discrimination affects only one aspect of a person's identity at any one time
options.zh: 歧视一次只会作用于一个人身份的某一个方面

questions.explanationEn: Intersectionality, a term introduced by Kimberlé Crenshaw, describes how systems of disadvantage overlap: an Indigenous woman with a disability does not face 'Indigenous barriers' plus 'women's barriers' plus 'disability barriers' as separate stacks, but a specific combined experience — for instance being disbelieved about pain in a way that neither a non-Indigenous disabled woman nor an Indigenous man would be. For a paramedic the point is practical: social determinants compound, so ask about the whole situation rather than filing the patient under one category, and expect that the person in front of you may have excellent reasons to distrust the system you represent.
questions.explanationZh: 「交叉性」一词由 Kimberlé Crenshaw 提出，描述的是各种不利处境体系如何相互叠加：一位带有残障的原住民女性面对的，不是「原住民的障碍」加「女性的障碍」加「残障的障碍」三摞分开的东西，而是一种特定的复合经历——例如她诉说疼痛时不被相信的方式，既不同于非原住民的残障女性，也不同于原住民男性。对护理员来说要点很实际：社会决定因素会复合叠加，所以要了解患者的整体处境，而不是把人归到某一个类别里；并且要预期眼前这个人完全可能有充分的理由不信任你所代表的系统。

questions.questionEn: A woman who arrived in Canada recently becomes distressed when you, a male paramedic, move to examine her chest for palpitations. What is the most culturally humble response?
questions.questionZh: 一位刚来加拿大不久的女性因心悸求助。当作为男性护理员的你准备检查她的胸部时，她明显不安。最体现文化谦逊的回应是什么？

options.en: Explain that in Canada examinations are done the same way for every patient, then proceed
options.zh: 解释在加拿大所有患者的检查方式都一样，然后继续

options.en: Skip the chest examination entirely so as not to offend her
options.zh: 为了不冒犯她，完全跳过胸部检查

options.en: Pause, ask what would make the exam comfortable, and proceed only with her agreement
options.zh: 停下来，问她怎样检查会舒服一些，在她同意后才进行

options.en: Ask her to describe her culture's rules so that you can look them up later
options.zh: 请她讲讲她的文化有哪些规矩，方便你以后查阅

questions.explanationEn: Cultural humility means asking rather than assuming: you do not need to know which tradition she comes from to notice distress and invite her to tell you what would help. The clinical need does not disappear — palpitations warrant cardiac assessment and a 12-lead — so the task is to adapt how it is done, not whether. Offering a same-sex provider, a chaperone and minimal exposure, explaining the purpose, and waiting for agreement respects both her dignity and her consent. Insisting that 'everyone is examined the same way' sacrifices the relationship and may end the assessment anyway; skipping an indicated examination sacrifices her safety; and turning the moment into a lesson about her culture serves your curiosity, not her care.
questions.explanationZh: 文化谦逊意味着去问而不是去猜：你不需要知道她来自哪种传统，也能察觉她的不安并请她告诉你怎样会好一些。临床需求并不会消失——心悸需要心脏评估和 12 导联——所以要调整的是「怎么做」，而不是「做不做」。提供同性别的操作者、陪同人员和最小暴露，解释检查目的，并等她同意，既尊重了她的尊严也尊重了她的知情同意。坚持「所有人都一样检查」会牺牲信任关系，而且评估很可能照样做不成；跳过有指征的检查牺牲的是她的安全；把这一刻变成学习她文化的课堂，满足的是你的好奇心，而不是她的照护。

questions.questionEn: En route to a call in a First Nations community your partner says, 'Probably just another drunk — no need to get the glucometer out for this one.' On arrival the patient is confused and sweating. What is the right response?
questions.questionZh: 前往一个原住民社区出诊的路上，搭档说：「八成又是个醉鬼——这单用不着拿血糖仪。」到达后患者意识模糊、出汗。正确的回应是什么？

options.en: Say nothing now and raise the comment at your partner's annual review
options.zh: 现在不说，等搭档年度考评时再提这句话

options.en: Go along with it to keep the crew relationship smooth for the rest of the shift
options.zh: 顺着他，让这个班剩下的时间车组关系融洽

options.en: Report your partner to the police for discrimination as soon as the call ends
options.zh: 这单一结束就以歧视为由向警方举报搭档

options.en: Assess fully yourself, speak up now, and raise it with him afterwards
options.zh: 自己做完整评估，当场表态，事后再和他谈

questions.explanationEn: Anti-racism is something you do, not something you merely believe: here a stereotype is about to shape an assessment, and confusion with sweating is a classic picture of hypoglycemia that a skipped glucose check could turn into a seizure or death. Patient safety comes first, so complete the assessment yourself and say plainly why. The conversation with your partner follows, privately; the Code of Ethics obliges you to report conduct that is incompetent or unethical through the proper authority, and a recurring pattern of this kind qualifies — your service's process is the right channel, not the police, since no criminal act has occurred. Waiting months lets the next patient pay for the delay, and going along makes you part of the harm the 'In Plain Sight' review described.
questions.explanationZh: 反种族主义是要做出来的，不只是心里认同：这里一句刻板印象正要左右一次评估，而意识模糊加出汗是低血糖的典型表现，漏掉一次血糖检测可能演变成抽搐甚至死亡。患者安全第一，所以你自己把评估做完，并直说为什么。与搭档的谈话随后私下进行；职业道德准则要求你通过正当途径举报不胜任或不道德的行为，这类反复出现的模式就属于此列——机构的流程才是正确渠道，不是警察，因为并没有发生刑事行为。拖到几个月后，代价由下一位患者承担；顺着他，你就成了《In Plain Sight》报告所描述的伤害的一部分。

questions.questionEn: A 68-year-old man who speaks little English needs to understand the risks of refusing transport after a fall in which he struck his head. His 10-year-old granddaughter offers to translate. The situation is not time-critical. What is the best approach?
questions.questionZh: 一位 68 岁、几乎不会英语的男性跌倒时撞到了头，现在需要理解拒绝转运的风险。他 10 岁的孙女主动提出翻译。情况并不紧急。最好的做法是什么？

options.en: Use the telephone interpreter service, speaking directly to the patient
options.zh: 使用电话口译服务，直接对患者说话

options.en: Let the granddaughter translate everything — she is fluent in both languages
options.zh: 让孙女翻译全部内容——她两种语言都流利

options.en: Use a translation app on your phone for the entire consent discussion
options.zh: 整个知情同意谈话都用手机翻译软件

options.en: Rely on gestures and on the fact that he nods along as you explain
options.zh: 靠手势，加上他在你解释时一直点头

questions.explanationEn: A refusal is only valid if the patient actually understands the risks, and a head strike in an older adult carries real ones — delayed intracranial bleeding among them. A child interpreter is unreliable for that task: she may lack the vocabulary, soften frightening information to protect her grandfather, or be burdened with news no child should carry, and the family hierarchy may stop him from speaking frankly through her. Professional interpreters are accurate, impartial and bound by confidentiality, and most services can reach one by phone within minutes; using the child for 'where does it hurt' while you connect is reasonable, but the consent conversation waits for the interpreter. Translation apps mishandle nuance and send health information to third-party servers. Nodding is a social reflex, not comprehension.
questions.explanationZh: 拒绝只有在患者真正理解风险时才有效，而老年人头部撞击的风险是实实在在的——包括迟发性颅内出血。让孩子当翻译在这件事上并不可靠：她可能缺乏相应词汇，可能为了保护祖父把吓人的信息说轻，可能被迫承受孩子不该承担的消息，而家庭长幼秩序也可能让他不愿通过她坦率表达。专业口译准确、中立并受保密约束，多数机构几分钟内就能电话接通；在接通期间让孩子问「哪里疼」是合理的，但知情同意的谈话要等口译。翻译软件处理不了细微差别，还会把健康信息发到第三方服务器。点头是社交反射，不代表理解。

questions.questionEn: Which obligation is written into the EMA Code of Ethics found in Schedule 3 of BC's Emergency Medical Assistants Regulation?
questions.questionZh: 下列哪项义务写进了 BC《Emergency Medical Assistants Regulation》附表 3 的 EMA 职业道德准则？

options.en: To communicate with each patient in that patient's first language
options.zh: 用每位患者的母语与其交流

options.en: To protect patient safety and dignity regardless of race, religion, disability or sex
options.zh: 无论种族、宗教、残疾或性别，都要保护患者的安全与尊严

options.en: To treat every patient identically, without adapting care to individual circumstances
options.zh: 对每位患者完全同等对待，不根据个人情况调整照护

options.en: To decline care to patients who behave disrespectfully toward the crew
options.zh: 对不尊重车组的患者可以拒绝提供照护

questions.explanationEn: The Code of Ethics lists the protected grounds explicitly and makes safety and dignity the duty — and because compliance with the Code is a condition of every licence under section 11 of the Regulation, discriminatory care is a licensing matter, not just a workplace one. The Code does not demand identical treatment; equitable care adapts to the person while refusing to discriminate against them. No one is expected to speak every language — the obligation is met by using interpreters. And the Code tells EMAs to place the patient's well-being above all, which rules out withholding care because someone was rude.
questions.explanationZh: 职业道德准则明确列出了受保护的事由，并把保护安全与尊严定为义务——由于依法规第 11 条遵守准则是每张执照的条件，歧视性照护属于执照问题，不只是职场问题。准则并不要求完全相同的对待；公平的照护是在拒绝歧视的同时根据个人情况调整。没有人被要求会说所有语言——这项义务通过使用口译来履行。准则还要求 EMA 把患者福祉置于一切之上，这就排除了因为对方无礼而拒绝照护。

questions.questionEn: A colleague says: 'I don't see colour — I treat everyone exactly the same, so I can't be part of the problem.' What is the strongest critique of this position?
questions.questionZh: 一位同事说：「我不看肤色——我对每个人都一模一样，所以问题不可能出在我身上。」对这种立场最有力的批评是什么？

options.en: It is correct — identical treatment is the very definition of fairness
options.zh: 他说得对——一模一样的对待正是公平的定义

options.en: It is wrong only because some patients genuinely prefer special treatment
options.zh: 之所以不对，只是因为有些患者确实偏好特殊待遇

options.en: 'The same' ignores patients' differing needs and lets unexamined bias keep working
options.zh: 「一模一样」忽视了患者各不相同的需求，让未经审视的偏见继续运作

options.en: It is only a problem in rural services, where crews know the patients
options.zh: 这只在车组认识患者的乡村机构才是问题

questions.explanationEn: Equality gives everyone the same thing; equity gives each person what they need to reach the same outcome. A patient who cannot read the discharge sheet, who distrusts hospitals because of what happened to their parents in an Indian hospital, or who has no way to fill a prescription needs different care to end up equally safe — identical care leaves them worse off. The 'colour-blind' claim also misunderstands bias: implicit bias operates whether or not we intend it, and the evidence from reviews such as 'In Plain Sight' is that it operates in BC. Declaring oneself exempt removes the self-reflection that cultural humility depends on. None of this is about patients wanting privileges, and it is not confined to any region.
questions.explanationZh: 平等（equality）是给每个人同样的东西；公平（equity）是给每个人达到同样结果所需要的东西。一个看不懂出院单的患者、一个因为父母在印第安医院的遭遇而不信任医院的患者、一个没办法去配药的患者，需要不同的照护才能获得同样的安全——完全相同的照护只会让他们更糟。「不看肤色」的说法还误解了偏见：内隐偏见不管我们是否有意都在运作，《In Plain Sight》之类的审查给出的证据是它就在 BC 运作着。宣布自己不在其列，恰恰取消了文化谦逊所依赖的自我反思。这一切与患者想要特权无关，也不局限于任何地区。

questions.questionEn: Call to Action 22 of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada asks those who can effect change in the health-care system to:
questions.questionZh: 加拿大真相与和解委员会（TRC）第 22 号行动呼吁要求医疗系统中能够推动改变的人做什么？

options.en: Replace conventional hospital care with traditional healing for all Indigenous patients
options.zh: 对所有原住民患者用传统疗愈取代常规医院治疗

options.en: Require every patient to declare Indigenous status at triage
options.zh: 要求每位患者在分诊时申报原住民身份

options.en: Close the segregated Indian hospitals that were still operating in 2015
options.zh: 关闭 2015 年仍在运营的种族隔离式印第安医院

options.en: Recognise Indigenous healing practices and use them when patients request
options.zh: 承认原住民疗愈实践，并在患者提出时加以运用

questions.explanationEn: The Commission's 2015 report devoted Calls to Action 18 to 24 to health. Number 22 asks the system to recognise Indigenous healing practices and make room for them, with healers and Elders, when patients ask; number 23 calls for more Indigenous health professionals and cultural-competency training for all health workers; number 24 asks medical and nursing schools to teach the history and legacy of residential schools, Indigenous rights and anti-racism. For a paramedic, Call 22 translates into concrete behaviour: ask, accommodate a smudge or a medicine bundle where safe, document it for the receiving team. The Call does not replace medical care or compel disclosure of identity, and the segregated Indian hospitals had closed by the early 1980s — their legacy, not their operation, is what shapes patient mistrust today.
questions.explanationZh: 委员会 2015 年的报告把第 18 至 24 号行动呼吁留给了健康领域。第 22 号要求医疗系统承认原住民疗愈实践，并在患者提出时与治疗师和长老合作为其留出空间；第 23 号呼吁增加原住民医疗从业者、并对所有医疗工作者进行文化胜任力培训；第 24 号要求医学院和护理学院讲授寄宿学校的历史与遗留影响、原住民权利和反种族主义。对护理员来说，第 22 号落实为具体行为：主动询问，在安全的前提下容许熏香（smudge）或药囊，并记录下来告知接收团队。这项呼吁既不取代医疗照护，也不强制申报身份；而种族隔离式的印第安医院早在 1980 年代初就已关闭——如今塑造患者不信任的是它们的遗留影响，而不是它们还在运营。

questions.questionEn: In the LEAPS de-escalation model, what does the 'P' stand for, and what does that step accomplish?
questions.questionZh: 在 LEAPS 危机降级模型中，「P」代表什么？这一步起什么作用？

options.en: Pause — give the person a deliberate moment of silence before replying
options.zh: Pause（停顿）——回应前刻意给对方一刻安静

options.en: Paraphrase — restate the substance of what was said, so it can be corrected
options.zh: Paraphrase（复述）——重述对方所说的实质内容，让对方可以纠正

options.en: Promise — commit to resolving the complaint before you leave the scene
options.zh: Promise（承诺）——保证离开现场前解决对方的投诉

options.en: Position — move to a tactically safer spot before continuing the conversation
options.zh: Position（站位）——继续谈话前先移到战术上更安全的位置

questions.explanationEn: LEAPS stands for Listen, Empathise, Ask, Paraphrase and Summarise. Paraphrasing is not parroting the words back; it is restating the substance — 'so the pharmacy closed before you could pick it up' — so the person hears that their message landed and can fix anything you got wrong. That alone often lowers the volume, because much of an angry person's escalation comes from feeling unheard. Summarising, the final step, pulls the agreed facts and the plan together. Pausing, promising outcomes you may not control, and tactical repositioning all have their place, but none of them is the P in LEAPS.
questions.explanationZh: LEAPS 是 Listen（倾听）、Empathise（共情）、Ask（提问）、Paraphrase（复述）、Summarise（总结）。复述不是鹦鹉学舌，而是把实质内容重新讲一遍——「所以药房在你赶到之前就关门了」——让对方听到自己的话被接收到了，并且可以纠正你说错的地方。单是这一步常常就能把音量降下来，因为愤怒者的升级很大一部分来自「没人听我说」。最后一步总结，是把双方认可的事实和计划归拢起来。停顿、承诺你未必掌控得了的结果、战术调整站位各有其用，但都不是 LEAPS 里的那个 P。

questions.questionEn: While you assess a woman at a bus loop, her companion falls silent, his face flushes, his jaw and fists tighten, he turns his body sideways to you and keeps glancing at your radio and then at your hands. How should you read this and respond?
questions.questionZh: 你在公交总站评估一名女性时，她的同伴突然不说话了，脸涨红，下颌和拳头绷紧，身体侧对着你，目光不停地扫过你的对讲机、再扫到你的手。该如何解读并应对？

options.en: He is anxious about his friend — carry on, and reassure him afterwards
options.zh: 他在为朋友担心——继续做事，过后安慰他

options.en: He is cold and tired of waiting — offer him a blanket and a seat in the warm ambulance
options.zh: 他冷了、等烦了——给他一条毯子，让他到暖和的车里坐

options.en: He is getting ready to leave — ignore him and keep working on the patient
options.zh: 他准备走了——不用理，继续处理患者

options.en: These are pre-assault cues — widen the gap, keep your exit clear, alert your partner
options.zh: 这些是攻击前征兆——拉开距离、保持退路畅通、提醒搭档

questions.explanationEn: Distress and threat look different. Fear and overload show as averted gaze, hand-wringing, trembling, pacing, crying and repeated questions — a stress reaction that responds to empathy and information. Preparation to attack shows as the cluster described here: scanning your weapons, hands or equipment ('target glancing'), turning side-on to present a smaller target and load a punch, clenched jaw and fists, flushing or sudden pallor, and the conversation going quiet. When you see that cluster, safety actions come before any further rapport-building — distance, a clear path out, a word to your partner, and a low threshold for leaving and requesting police. Misreading it as worry, cold or boredom removes the seconds you would need.
questions.explanationZh: 痛苦和威胁的样子不一样。恐惧和超负荷表现为回避目光、搓手、发抖、来回走动、哭泣、反复追问——那是应激反应，对共情和信息有回应。准备动手则表现为题干里这一组征兆：扫视你的武器、手或装备（「目标扫视」）、侧身以缩小受击面并蓄力出拳、下颌和拳头绷紧、脸色涨红或骤然发白、对话突然沉下去。看到这组征兆，安全动作要排在继续建立关系之前——拉开距离、留出退路、知会搭档，并把撤离和呼叫警察的门槛放低。把它误读成担心、受凉或不耐烦，会把你需要的那几秒钟白白丢掉。

questions.questionEn: A man is shouting that his mother has been waiting for help for two hours and that 'nobody cares'. Which reply best demonstrates the Empathise step of LEAPS?
questions.questionZh: 一名男子大喊他母亲等了两个小时都没人来帮忙，「根本没人在乎」。哪句回应最能体现 LEAPS 中的「共情」一步？

options.en: 'Two hours with your mum unwell and no one telling you anything — I'd be angry too.'
options.zh: 「妈妈不舒服等了两个小时，没人跟你们说一声——换我也会生气。」

options.en: 'Sir, you need to lower your voice right now, or we are not going to be able to help you.'
options.zh: 「先生，你现在就得把声音放低，不然我们没办法帮你。」

options.en: 'Response times aren't my department — you'd have to take that up with dispatch.'
options.zh: 「响应时间不归我管——你得去找调度中心说。」

options.en: 'Well, there are other people waiting as well, and we got here as fast as we could.'
options.zh: 「可是还有别人也在等啊，我们已经尽快赶来了。」

questions.explanationEn: Empathising means naming the feeling and the reason for it in a way the person recognises as true, without agreeing to blame or promising what you cannot deliver. 'I'd be angry too' validates the emotion, and a follow-up such as 'I'm here now — tell me what's been happening' moves straight into Listen and Ask. A command to lower his voice is heard as a threat and usually raises the volume; deflecting responsibility and comparing him to other patients both communicate that his mother does not matter — the exact belief that is fuelling the shouting.
questions.explanationZh: 共情是把对方的感受和产生这种感受的原因说出来，让他觉得被说中了，同时既不替谁认错，也不承诺做不到的事。「换我也会生气」承认了情绪；接一句「我现在到了，跟我说说情况」就直接进入倾听和提问。命令他放低声音会被听成威胁，通常只会让音量更高；推卸责任和拿别的患者作比较，传达的都是「你母亲不重要」——恰恰是让他大喊的那个念头。

questions.questionEn: Which positioning best balances rapport with safety when you are speaking with an agitated patient in his living room?
questions.questionZh: 在客厅里与一名激动的患者交谈时，哪种站位最能兼顾关系建立和安全？

options.en: Squarely in front of him and within arm's reach, to project calm confidence
options.zh: 正对着他、在一臂之内，以显示沉着自信

options.en: Between him and the only door, so that he cannot leave before you finish
options.zh: 挡在他和唯一的门之间，让他在你完成前走不了

options.en: At a slight angle, beyond two arm's lengths, with your own exit route kept clear
options.zh: 略呈角度、站在两臂之外，自己的退路保持畅通

options.en: Behind him and to one side, so that he cannot see your equipment or radio
options.zh: 站在他身后偏侧，让他看不到你的装备和对讲机

questions.explanationEn: Standing slightly angled rather than square-on reads as less confrontational and also presents a smaller target. Two arm's lengths is the reactionary gap — the distance that gives you time to react to a sudden strike or grab. Your exit must stay open: an agitated person who moves between you and the door has changed the situation, and that is a cue to reposition or leave. Blocking the patient's own way out does the opposite of de-escalation, because feeling trapped is one of the strongest triggers for violence. Approaching from behind startles people and removes your view of their hands.
questions.explanationZh: 略呈角度而不是正对面站立，给人的对抗感更弱，也缩小了受击面。两臂的距离就是反应间距——让你来得及对突然的击打或抓扯做出反应。你的退路必须保持畅通：一个激动的人移动到你和门之间，局面就变了，这是重新站位或离开的信号。挡住患者自己的出路则与降级背道而驰，因为「被困住」的感觉是暴力最强的触发因素之一。从身后接近会吓到对方，还让你看不到他的双手。

questions.questionEn: A 15-year-old on the autism spectrum has become agitated after a brief seizure. The living room has a loud television, four relatives talking at once and a glaring overhead light. Which first adjustment is most likely to help?
questions.questionZh: 一名 15 岁自闭症谱系少年在一次短暂抽搐后变得躁动。客厅里电视声很大、四位亲属同时在说话、顶灯刺眼。先做哪项调整最可能有帮助？

options.en: Start the physical examination quickly so you can get him out of the room sooner
options.zh: 尽快开始体格检查，好早点把他带出这个房间

options.en: TV off, lights down, one relative stays, one paramedic speaks in a low voice
options.zh: 关电视、调暗灯、只留一位亲属、一名护理员低声交流

options.en: Speak louder than the television so that he can hear your instructions clearly
options.zh: 声音盖过电视，让他听清你的指令

options.en: Have both paramedics give instructions at the same time to save time
options.zh: 两名护理员同时下指令以节省时间

questions.explanationEn: Agitation after a seizure is often driven by sensory overload and confusion, and for an autistic adolescent noise, light and several competing voices can be overwhelming in themselves. Reducing stimulation — one quiet voice, dimmer light, fewer people — removes the fuel before you ask anything of him. Keeping the one relative who knows him best gives you his baseline, his communication preferences and a familiar face. Rushing into a hands-on examination, shouting over the television or having two people issue instructions all add stimulation and are likely to escalate rather than calm him; the examination follows once he is settled, with permission asked step by step.
questions.explanationZh: 抽搐后的躁动常常由感官超载和意识混乱驱动，而对自闭症谱系的少年来说，噪音、强光和几个人同时说话本身就足以压垮他。先降低刺激——一个安静的声音、更暗的光、更少的人——是在向他提任何要求之前先撤掉燃料。留下最了解他的那位亲属，能提供他的基线状态、沟通偏好和一张熟悉的面孔。急着上手检查、扯着嗓子盖过电视、两个人同时下指令，都是在增加刺激，更可能让他升级而不是平静；等他安定下来再做检查，每一步都先征得同意。

questions.questionEn: A woman who was assaulted last year flinches whenever you reach toward her and says she 'hates being handled'. Which approach best restores her sense of control?
questions.questionZh: 一位去年遭受过暴力侵害的女性，每当你伸手靠近就会瑟缩，说她「最讨厌被人摆弄」。哪种做法最能恢复她的掌控感？

options.en: Offer real choices and ask permission before each step, such as which arm
options.zh: 给出真实的选择，每一步前先征得同意，比如用哪只手臂

options.en: Tell her exactly what you are going to do and then do it — predictability is enough
options.zh: 准确告诉她你要做什么然后就做——有可预期性就够了

options.en: Ask her to decide the whole order of the assessment herself, from start to finish
options.zh: 让她自己从头到尾决定整个评估的顺序

options.en: Reassure her that you are a professional and that she has nothing to fear
options.zh: 安慰她你是专业人员，没什么好怕的

questions.explanationEn: Trauma-informed care rests on safety, trustworthiness, choice, collaboration and empowerment. Small, genuine choices — which arm, whether to sit or lie, whether a support person stays — hand control back to someone whose control was taken from her, and asking before each touch turns you from a threat into a partner. Narrating your actions is helpful but keeps all the control with you. Asking her to run the whole assessment overloads her and hides the fact that some things must happen in a certain order. Telling her she has nothing to fear dismisses a fear that, given her history, is entirely reasonable.
questions.explanationZh: 创伤知情照护建立在安全、可信、选择、协作和赋权之上。微小但真实的选择——哪只手臂、坐着还是躺着、要不要留一位陪伴者——把掌控感还给一个曾被夺走掌控感的人；每次触碰前先问，把你从威胁变成了同伴。叙述你的动作有帮助，但掌控权仍全在你手里。让她安排整个评估会把她压垮，也掩盖了有些步骤必须按顺序进行的事实。告诉她没什么好怕的，是在否定一种以她的经历来看完全合理的恐惧。

questions.questionEn: During a mental-health call in a small kitchen, the patient stops answering your calm questions, steps between you and the hallway, opens a drawer and takes out a hammer, saying, 'Nobody's taking me anywhere.' What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 一次精神健康出诊，在狭小的厨房里，患者不再回答你平静的提问，走到你和走廊之间，拉开抽屉拿出一把锤子，说：「谁也别想把我带走。」你该怎么做？

options.en: Keep talking in a calm voice — verbal de-escalation works if you persist long enough
options.zh: 继续用平静的声音说话——只要坚持得够久，语言降级就会起效

options.en: Move closer with your hands open and visible to show that you are not a threat
options.zh: 张开双手、让他看见，走近表明你没有威胁

options.en: Try to take the hammer away from him before he has a chance to use it
options.zh: 趁他还没机会动手，先把锤子夺下来

options.en: Break contact, get out by any open route, and call police from a safe place
options.zh: 中断接触，从任何可用的路线离开，到安全地点呼叫警察

questions.explanationEn: Verbal de-escalation has limits, and this scene has crossed all of them at once: a weapon in hand, your exit blocked and an explicit threat. That is an active threat, not a stress reaction, and the correct response is withdrawal: break off the conversation, put space and an obstacle between you, cue your partner, leave by whatever route is open — equipment stays behind if it must — and call for help once you are safe. Persisting with talk assumes a rationality he is not showing; closing the distance puts you inside hammer range; attempting to disarm him is a fight you are not trained or equipped for. Re-entry happens only with police present, and the mental-health concern is addressed once everyone is safe.
questions.explanationZh: 语言降级是有极限的，而这个场景一下子越过了全部极限：手里有武器、你的退路被堵、还有明确的威胁。这是主动威胁，不是应激反应，正确的应对是撤离：中断对话，在你们之间留出空间和障碍物，示意搭档，从任何可用的路线离开——必要时装备留在原地——到安全后再呼救。继续说话是在假设一种他并未表现出的理性；缩短距离等于把自己送进锤子的攻击范围；试图夺械是一场你既没受过训练也没有装备去打的架。装备可以再买。只有在警察到场后才重新进入，精神健康问题等所有人都安全了再处理。

questions.questionEn: Compared with a calm patient, how does an agitated person's need for personal space typically change, and what follows for your approach?
questions.questionZh: 和平静的患者相比，情绪激动的人对个人空间的需求通常会怎样变化？这对你的接近方式意味着什么？

options.en: It shrinks — moving in close shows that you care about what is happening to them
options.zh: 会缩小——凑近表示你在乎他们的遭遇

options.en: It stays the same — about half a metre is comfortable for almost everyone
options.zh: 不变——半米左右几乎对谁都舒服

options.en: It expands, often to two arm's lengths or more — approach slowly and ask before touching
options.zh: 会扩大，常到两臂甚至更远——慢慢接近，触碰前先询问

options.en: It stops mattering once you have identified yourself as a paramedic
options.zh: 一旦你表明自己是护理员，就不再重要

questions.explanationEn: In ordinary conversation most people tolerate others at roughly half a metre to a metre; under stress or anger that comfort zone grows, and someone entering it is experienced as a threat that triggers fight-or-flight. Watching for the first signs of discomfort — leaning back, stepping away, stiffening — and stopping there lets the patient set the distance. The same distance protects you, since two arm's lengths is also the reactionary gap. A uniform does not shrink the zone; for people with past bad experiences of authority it may enlarge it further.
questions.explanationZh: 日常交谈中，多数人能接受别人在半米到一米左右；在压力或愤怒之下，这个舒适区会扩大，有人闯进来就会被当成威胁，触发「战或逃」反应。留意最初的不适迹象——后仰、后退、身体僵硬——并在那里停下，让患者来决定距离。同样的距离也在保护你，因为两臂的距离正是反应间距。制服并不会缩小这个区域；对那些曾在权威面前有过糟糕经历的人来说，反而可能让它更大。

questions.questionEn: Which set of your own non-verbal behaviours is most likely to lower tension with a frightened, angry patient?
questions.questionZh: 面对一位又怕又怒的患者，你自己的哪一组非语言行为最可能降低紧张？

options.en: Arms folded, sunglasses on, standing over him while he remains seated
options.zh: 双臂交叉、戴着墨镜、他坐着而你居高临下地站着

options.en: Open hands at waist height, relaxed shoulders, slight angle, near his eye level
options.zh: 双手张开置于腰部、肩膀放松、略呈角度、接近他的视线高度

options.en: Hands clasped behind your back, chest squared to him, steady unbroken eye contact
options.zh: 双手背在身后、胸口正对着他、目光一直盯着不移开

options.en: Pointing at him to drive home each instruction, speaking slowly and firmly
options.zh: 用手指着他强调每条指令，语速缓慢而坚定

questions.explanationEn: Visible, open hands say 'no weapon and no surprise'; relaxed shoulders and slow movements signal that you are not about to act against him; a slight angle is less confrontational than squaring up; and bringing your eyes level with his removes the dominance of standing over a seated person — provided your route out stays clear. Folded arms and sunglasses hide you and read as closed or judging. Hands behind the back conceal them (alarming to a frightened person) and leave you unable to protect yourself. An unbroken stare is a challenge in most cultures, and pointing is one of the most universally aggressive gestures there is.
questions.explanationZh: 可见、张开的双手在说「没有武器、没有突袭」；放松的肩膀和缓慢的动作表明你不会突然对他做什么；略呈角度比正面相对少了对抗感；把视线降到和他齐平，则消除了站着俯视一个坐着的人所带来的压迫——前提是你的退路保持畅通。双臂交叉和墨镜把你藏了起来，读起来像封闭或审视。双手背在身后既藏起了手（对害怕的人来说很吓人），也让你无法自卫。一直盯着不放在多数文化里都是挑衅，而用手指人是最普遍的攻击性手势之一。

questions.questionEn: After listening to a long, angry account about cancelled appointments, you say: 'So — the clinic cancelled twice, your prescription ran out on Friday, and you've had no medication for three days, which is why you feel so unwell. Have I got that right?' Which LEAPS step is this, and why does it matter?
questions.questionZh: 听完患者关于预约被取消的一长段愤怒叙述后，你说：「所以——诊所取消了两次，你的处方药周五就吃完了，已经三天没药，所以才这么难受。我理解得对吗？」这是 LEAPS 的哪一步？为什么重要？

options.en: Listen — you are demonstrating that you heard the whole account
options.zh: 倾听——你在表明自己听完了整段叙述

options.en: Empathise — you are naming the emotion behind what he has told you
options.zh: 共情——你在说出他叙述背后的情绪

options.en: Paraphrase — you reflect his account back and check it with him
options.zh: 复述——你把他的叙述反馈回去并与他核对

options.en: Summarise — you are closing the conversation with the agreed plan
options.zh: 总结——你在用双方认可的计划收尾

questions.explanationEn: This is paraphrasing: his story, compressed and reflected back, ending with an invitation to correct you. It works because an escalating person repeats and amplifies until they believe the message has landed; a check question gives them proof. Listening is what you did while he spoke; empathising would name the feeling ('that's exhausting and frightening'); summarising comes last and covers what you have agreed to do next — 'so we'll take you in, and I'll tell them about the three missed days.' Keeping the steps distinct helps you notice when you have skipped one.
questions.explanationZh: 这是复述：把他的叙述浓缩后反馈回去，最后请他纠正。它之所以有效，是因为情绪升级的人会不断重复、不断加码，直到相信对方真的听懂了；一句核对的话就是证据。倾听是他说话时你在做的事；共情是说出感受（「这又累又吓人」）；总结放在最后，讲的是接下来双方同意怎么做——「那我们送你去医院，我会把三天没药的事告诉他们。」把各步分清楚，你才会察觉自己有没有跳过某一步。

questions.questionEn: While you treat a woman with chest pain, her adult son paces the room, breathes fast and keeps shouting, 'Do something — why are you so slow?' He has threatened no one. What is the best response?
questions.questionZh: 你正在处理一位胸痛的女性，她的成年儿子在房间里来回走、呼吸急促，不停地喊：「快想想办法——你们怎么这么慢？」他没有威胁任何人。最好的回应是什么？

options.en: Treat it as a stress reaction: brief acknowledgement, short updates, a concrete task
options.zh: 当作应激反应处理：简短承认、不时简要更新、给一件具体的事做

options.en: Have your partner escort him out of the house and keep him outside until the patient is packaged
options.zh: 让搭档把他请出屋子，在患者打包好之前一直留在外面

options.en: Ignore him completely and work faster so that you can leave sooner
options.zh: 完全不理他，加快动作早点离开

options.en: Call the police to remove him from the scene before you continue care
options.zh: 先叫警察把他带离现场，再继续处置

questions.explanationEn: Pacing, rapid breathing and demands for action are the signature of fear and helplessness, not of intent to harm. The remedy is information and a role: a sentence acknowledging his fear, brief running commentary ('we've done the ECG, we're giving her aspirin now'), and a task that both helps you and channels his energy. Ejecting him or calling police treats a frightened son as a threat, loses a valuable source of history and may tip him into real hostility. Ignoring him leaves the anxiety to grow in the background. Keep watching, though — if his cues shift toward threat (clenched fists, moving into your space, personal threats), the response changes.
questions.explanationZh: 来回踱步、呼吸急促、催促行动，是恐惧和无助的典型表现，不是伤人的意图。对策是信息加角色：一句话承认他的担心，简短的实时解说（「心电图做完了，现在给她吃阿司匹林」），再给他一件既帮到你、又能释放他能量的任务。把他赶出去或叫警察，是把一个受惊的儿子当成了威胁，既失去了宝贵的病史来源，还可能把他推向真正的敌意。不理他，焦虑只会在背景里继续膨胀。不过要持续观察——如果他的信号转向威胁（握拳、闯入你的空间、针对个人的威胁），应对就要变。

questions.questionEn: A 30-year-old man is terrified because voices are telling him that paramedics are 'coming to harvest his organs'. He is not aggressive. Which approach is most likely to keep him calm and allow an assessment?
questions.questionZh: 一名 30 岁男性极度惊恐，因为有声音告诉他护理员是「来摘他器官的」。他没有攻击性。哪种做法最可能让他保持平静并接受评估？

options.en: Tell him firmly that the voices are not real and that he must stop talking about them
options.zh: 坚定地告诉他那些声音不是真的，不许再说了

options.en: Play along — agree the voices might be right, but promise to protect him from the harvesters
options.zh: 顺着他说——承认那些声音可能是对的，但保证会保护他不被摘器官

options.en: Avoid speaking to him at all and leave the conversation entirely to the police
options.zh: 完全不和他说话，把交谈全交给警察

options.en: Acknowledge the fear without arguing or agreeing, move slowly, and rule out medical causes
options.zh: 承认他的恐惧但不争论也不认同，动作放慢，并排除医学原因

questions.explanationEn: You cannot argue someone out of a psychotic belief, and trying to confirms that you are an adversary. Colluding with it is dishonest and reinforces the delusion — and a promise to 'protect him from the harvesters' will be remembered when you later insist on transport. The workable path is to validate the emotion, which is real, while staying neutral about its content; to be transparent and slow; and to earn consent for each step. Hand the conversation to police only if safety requires it — the therapeutic relationship is yours to build. And keep clinical: new or worsening psychosis has medical mimics (hypoglycemia, stimulant or hallucinogen use, sepsis, head injury), so a glucose check and a full assessment are part of calming him, not separate from it.
questions.explanationZh: 你无法用争辩把一个人从精神病性信念里拉出来，而争辩只会证实你是敌人。附和它则是不诚实的，还会强化妄想——况且「保护你不被摘器官」的承诺，会在你稍后坚持转运时被他记起来。可行的路径是承认那份真实存在的情绪，同时对其内容保持中立；做到透明和缓慢；每一步都争取同意。只有在安全需要时才把交谈交给警察——治疗关系要靠你自己建立。同时别忘了临床：新发或加重的精神病性症状有医学上的「冒充者」（低血糖、兴奋剂或致幻剂、脓毒症、头部外伤），所以测血糖和完整评估是安抚他的一部分，不是另一件事。

questions.questionEn: Which statement best captures the difference between health equity and health equality?
questions.questionZh: 下列哪项最准确地说明了健康公平（equity）与健康平等（equality）的区别？

options.en: Equity matches resources to need so outcomes can match; equality gives everyone the same
options.zh: 公平是按需要分配资源以求结果相当；平等是给每个人同样的东西

options.en: Equality is the legal standard in Canada; equity is a voluntary professional ideal with no legal footing
options.zh: 平等是加拿大的法律标准；公平只是没有法律依据的自愿职业理想

options.en: Equity means spending more on hospitals; equality means spending more on prevention programs
options.zh: 公平指多在医院上花钱；平等指多在预防项目上花钱

options.en: Equality applies to individual patients; equity applies only to population-level planning
options.zh: 平等适用于个体患者；公平只适用于人群层面的规划

questions.explanationEn: Equality hands every person the same thing — the same pamphlet, the same ten minutes, the same instructions in English. Equity recognises that people start from different places and gives each what they need to reach a comparable outcome: an interpreter for one, extra time for another, help getting a prescription filled for a third. The distinction operates at every level, from a single patient encounter to provincial planning, so neither term is confined to one scale. It is also not a hospital-versus-prevention budget question. And equity has real legal and professional footing in BC: the EMA Code of Ethics requires protecting every patient's safety and dignity regardless of protected characteristics, and human-rights law requires reasonable accommodation.
questions.explanationZh: 平等是给每个人同样的东西——同一本小册子、同样的十分钟、同样的英文说明。公平则承认人们的起点不同，给每个人达到相当结果所需要的东西：给这位配口译，给那位多一点时间，帮第三位把处方配到手。这个区别在每个层面都成立，从一次患者接触到全省规划，所以哪个词都不只限于某一个尺度。它也不是「医院还是预防」的预算问题。而且公平在 BC 有实实在在的法律和职业依据：EMA 职业道德准则要求无论受保护特征如何都要保护每位患者的安全与尊严，人权法也要求合理便利。

questions.questionEn: A single mother in a rural BC town brings her son to the ED by ambulance for the third asthma flare this season. She has no car, the nearest pharmacy is 40 minutes away by a bus that runs twice a day, and her job offers no paid sick leave. Which action addresses an upstream determinant rather than the immediate symptom?
questions.questionZh: BC 乡村小镇的一位单身母亲，这个季节第三次叫救护车送儿子因哮喘发作去急诊。她没有车，最近的药房坐一天只有两班的公交要 40 分钟，工作也没有带薪病假。哪项行动针对的是上游决定因素，而不是眼前的症状？

options.en: Give salbutamol by MDI with spacer and reassess the child's work of breathing
options.zh: 用带储雾罐的定量吸入器给沙丁胺醇，并复评孩子的呼吸做功

options.en: Link the family to community paramedicine or social work for medication and transport help
options.zh: 为这家人联系社区护理员或社工，解决取药和交通问题

options.en: Give the mother a printed asthma action plan and tell her to review it with the family doctor
options.zh: 给母亲一份打印的哮喘行动计划，让她和家庭医生一起过一遍

options.en: Advise her to call 911 earlier next time so that treatment can start before he is this unwell
options.zh: 建议她下次早点打 911，好在孩子病得这么重之前就开始治疗

questions.explanationEn: The boy keeps relapsing because the controller medication is hard to collect and the household has no slack to manage illness — those are social determinants (transportation, income and employment conditions, health-care access), and they sit upstream of every exacerbation. Linking the family with community paramedicine, a social worker or a pharmacy delivery program acts on that cause. The bronchodilator is correct and necessary, but it is the downstream treatment; a written action plan is useful education that still assumes she can obtain the medication; and telling her to call sooner shifts the burden back onto her while leaving the barrier untouched. Document the referral and her response to it so the next crew and the receiving team can follow through.
questions.explanationZh: 孩子反复发作，是因为控制药物难以取得、这个家庭也没有余力应对生病——这些是社会决定因素（交通、收入和就业条件、医疗可及性），处在每一次发作的上游。为这家人联系社区护理员、社工或药房送药项目，针对的正是这个根源。给支气管扩张剂是正确且必要的，但那是下游的治疗；书面行动计划是有用的教育，却仍然默认她拿得到药；让她早点打电话，是把负担推回给她，而障碍一点没动。把转介和她的回应记录下来，让下一个车组和接收团队能够跟进。

questions.questionEn: Why do health-literacy experts recommend plain language with every patient, rather than only with those who seem to need it?
questions.questionZh: 健康素养专家为什么建议对每一位患者都用大白话，而不是只对看起来需要的人这样做？

options.en: Because plain language is required by the EMALB documentation standard for all verbal instructions to patients
options.zh: 因为 EMALB 的文书标准要求对患者的所有口头指导都使用大白话

options.en: Because most patients with low literacy will tell you so if you ask them directly at the start
options.zh: 因为大多数读写能力有限的患者，只要一开始直接问，都会告诉你

options.en: Because clinical terminology is legally protected and may only be used between licensed clinicians
options.zh: 因为临床术语受法律保护，只能在持牌医护之间使用

options.en: Because around 60% of Canadian adults have limited health literacy, and you cannot tell who by looking
options.zh: 因为大约六成加拿大成年人健康素养有限，而且看外表根本分辨不出是谁

questions.explanationEn: Canadian survey data have long estimated that roughly six in ten adults — and nearly nine in ten seniors — lack the health literacy needed to understand and act on health information. Limited literacy does not show on the surface, and people commonly hide it out of embarrassment, nodding rather than admitting confusion. That is why the recommended approach is 'universal precautions': short sentences, everyday words, one idea at a time and a teach-back check for everyone. No EMALB documentation rule dictates the vocabulary of your spoken instructions, and clinical terminology is not legally restricted — it is simply the wrong tool for most patients.
questions.explanationZh: 加拿大的调查数据长期估计，大约六成成年人——老年人接近九成——缺乏理解并据以行动的健康素养。素养有限从表面看不出来，人们还常因难为情而掩饰，宁可点头也不承认没听懂。所以推荐的做法是「普遍预防」：短句、日常用词、一次只讲一件事，并对所有人做复述确认。EMALB 没有哪条文书规则规定你口头指导的用词；临床术语也不受法律限制——它只是对大多数患者而言用错了工具。

questions.questionEn: You have treated a man's hypoglycemia with oral glucose and he will stay at home. Which wording best uses teach-back to confirm that he understood your instructions?
questions.questionZh: 你用口服葡萄糖处理了一名男性的低血糖，他将留在家中。哪种说法最能用「复述确认」（teach-back）来核实他理解了你的指导？

options.en: 'Do you understand what I told you about eating something and rechecking your sugar in a little while?'
options.zh: 「我刚才说的——吃点东西、过一会儿再测血糖——你都明白了吗？」

options.en: 'So I know I explained it well — what will you eat now, and when will you recheck your sugar?'
options.zh: 「为了确认我讲清楚了——你现在打算吃什么？什么时候再测血糖？」

options.en: 'Any questions about what we talked about? No? Great — the instruction sheet has everything in writing.'
options.zh: 「对刚才说的还有问题吗？没有？好——说明单上都写着。」

options.en: 'Repeat back to me exactly what I said, word for word, so I can confirm you were listening properly.'
options.zh: 「把我说的话一字不差地重复一遍，好让我确认你刚才有在听。」

questions.explanationEn: Teach-back puts the responsibility on the explainer, not the patient: 'so I know I explained it well' frames the check as a test of your teaching, and asking him to say in his own words what he will eat and when he will recheck shows you whether the plan actually landed. A yes/no question ('do you understand?') is almost always answered yes, whatever was understood. 'Any questions?' followed by a leaflet assumes he can and will read it, which many patients cannot. Demanding a word-for-word repetition is a memory test that shames the patient and proves nothing about comprehension. Record what he was able to explain back; that documentation is part of a defensible decision to leave him at home.
questions.explanationZh: 复述确认把责任放在解释者而不是患者身上：「为了确认我讲清楚了」把这次核对定位成对你讲解的检验；请他用自己的话说出要吃什么、何时复测，才能看出计划是否真的被理解。「明白了吗」这种是非问句，不管听懂多少几乎都会答「明白」。「还有问题吗」加一张说明单，默认他能读、也会读，而很多患者做不到。要求一字不差地复述是记忆测试，既让患者难堪，也证明不了理解。把他能复述出来的内容记录下来；这份记录是让他留在家中这一决定站得住脚的一部分。

questions.questionEn: At a community health fair your crew offers free blood-pressure and blood-glucose checks to adults who have never been diagnosed with hypertension or diabetes. Which level of prevention is this?
questions.questionZh: 在社区健康日活动上，你们车组为从未被诊断过高血压或糖尿病的成年人提供免费血压和血糖检测。这属于哪一级预防？

options.en: Primary prevention — it stops the disease process from ever starting
options.zh: 一级预防——阻止疾病过程的发生

options.en: Tertiary prevention — it limits complications in people already diagnosed
options.zh: 三级预防——减少已确诊者的并发症

options.en: Secondary prevention — it detects disease early, before symptoms appear
options.zh: 二级预防——在出现症状之前早期发现疾病

options.en: Quaternary prevention — it protects people from unnecessary medical intervention
options.zh: 四级预防——保护人们免受不必要的医疗干预

questions.explanationEn: Screening people who have no diagnosis in order to catch disease before it declares itself is secondary prevention. Primary prevention acts before the disease exists at all — immunisation, smoking-cessation advice, fall-proofing a home. Tertiary prevention reduces the damage of established disease, such as cardiac rehabilitation after a heart attack or foot care for a person with diabetes. Quaternary prevention is the newer idea of protecting patients from over-investigation and over-treatment. Paramedics touch all four: a glucose or blood-pressure check at a community event is screening, while the referral conversation that follows an abnormal reading is where advocacy begins.
questions.explanationZh: 为尚无诊断的人筛查，赶在疾病显现之前把它找出来，就是二级预防。一级预防在疾病根本还不存在时就行动——免疫接种、戒烟建议、给住所做防跌倒改造。三级预防是减轻已有疾病造成的损害，比如心梗后的心脏康复、糖尿病患者的足部护理。四级预防是较新的概念，指保护患者免于过度检查和过度治疗。护理员四级都会碰到：社区活动上的血糖或血压检测是筛查，而读数异常之后的转介谈话，才是倡导的起点。

questions.questionEn: After a minor fall, a 70-year-old man with capacity declines transport. He mentions he has been skipping meals because his pension runs out mid-month and he does not know where to turn. Which number should you give him for information on food banks, subsidised housing and other community services in BC?
questions.questionZh: 一位 70 岁、有行为能力的男性轻微跌倒后拒绝转运。他提到自己一直在省饭吃，因为养老金月中就花光了，也不知道该找谁。关于 BC 的食物银行、补贴住房和其他社区服务信息，你该给他哪个号码？

options.en: 2-1-1 (bc211), the province-wide community and social services information line
options.zh: 2-1-1（bc211），全省范围的社区与社会服务信息热线

options.en: 8-1-1 (HealthLink BC), the 24-hour nurse and health information line
options.zh: 8-1-1（HealthLink BC），24 小时护士与健康信息热线

options.en: 9-8-8, the national suicide crisis helpline by call or text
options.zh: 9-8-8，全国自杀危机热线，可拨打或发短信

options.en: 3-1-1, the municipal services line for bylaws and local programs
options.zh: 3-1-1，市政服务热线，处理附例和本地项目

questions.explanationEn: bc211 is the province-wide information and referral service for community, social and government programs — food banks, housing supports, income assistance, seniors' services and more — reached by dialling 2-1-1 or online. HealthLink BC at 8-1-1 is the right call for a health question (a nurse around the clock, a pharmacist in the evening, a dietitian by appointment), and is worth mentioning as well, but it is not a social-services directory. 9-8-8 is Canada's suicide crisis line and belongs in a different conversation unless he shows risk. 3-1-1 handles municipal matters. Knowing these numbers lets a crew act on a social need found during a medical call; record the referral you made and what he said about it.
questions.explanationZh: bc211 是全省范围的社区、社会和政府项目信息与转介服务——食物银行、住房支持、收入援助、老年人服务等——拨 2-1-1 或上网即可。8-1-1 的 HealthLink BC 适合健康问题（护士全天候、晚间有药师、预约可找营养师），也值得一并告诉他，但它不是社会服务目录。9-8-8 是加拿大的自杀危机热线，除非他显示出风险，否则属于另一种谈话。3-1-1 处理市政事务。记住这些号码，车组才能对出诊中发现的社会需求采取行动；把你做的转介和他的回应记录下来。

questions.questionEn: An 81-year-old man with capacity refuses transport after you treat a minor hand burn. His apartment is cold, the fridge holds only condiments, his insulin sits on a warm windowsill, and he says his family 'doesn't bother anymore'. What is the most appropriate disposition?
questions.questionZh: 你处理了一位 81 岁男性的轻度手部烧伤，他有行为能力并拒绝转运。他的公寓很冷，冰箱里只有调味品，胰岛素放在温热的窗台上，他说家人「早就不管了」。最恰当的处置是什么？

options.en: Accept the refusal, complete the PCR, and advise him to call 911 again if anything changes
options.zh: 接受拒绝，写完 PCR，告诉他情况有变就再打 911

options.en: Transport him against his wishes, because the living conditions make the refusal unsafe
options.zh: 违背他的意愿转运，因为居住条件让这个拒绝不安全

options.en: Report him to the police as a vulnerable adult so they can decide whether he can stay
options.zh: 以弱势成年人为由向警方报告，由警方决定他能否留下

options.en: Honour the refusal, arrange the referrals he accepts, and report the living conditions
options.zh: 尊重拒绝，安排他接受的转介，并上报居住状况

questions.explanationEn: A capable adult's refusal of transport stands, and capacity is not removed by poverty or a cold flat — so transporting him against his will is unlawful, and police have no role when no crime or immediate danger exists. But leaving with a PCR and a 'call us again' abandons a man whose insulin is spoiling and whose next call may be a hypoglycemic collapse. The equitable disposition keeps his autonomy and acts on the risks: offer and arrange what he will accept (community paramedicine where available, HealthLink BC 8-1-1, bc211 at 2-1-1 for food and heating supports, a request that his physician or pharmacist review the insulin storage), and use your service's pathway to report the conditions — in BC the regional health authority is the designated agency under the Adult Guardianship Act for adults who may be unable to seek help themselves. Document each offer and his response to it, including his stated reasons.
questions.explanationZh: 一位有行为能力的成年人拒绝转运是有效的，贫穷或房子冷并不剥夺行为能力——所以违背意愿转运是违法的；在没有犯罪、没有即时危险时，警察也无从介入。但是留下一份 PCR 和一句「有事再打」，等于丢下一个胰岛素正在变质、下一通电话可能就是低血糖倒地的人。兼顾公平的处置是既保住他的自主，又对风险采取行动：提供并安排他愿意接受的（有条件的地区转介社区护理员、HealthLink BC 8-1-1、bc211 的 2-1-1 查食物和取暖补助、请他的医生或药师复核胰岛素储存），并通过机构的渠道上报居住状况——在 BC，依据《Adult Guardianship Act》，地区卫生局是负责处理可能无法自行求助的成年人情况的指定机构。把每一项提议和他的回应（包括他说的理由）都记录下来。

questions.questionEn: In British Columbia, which body is designated to receive and respond to reports that a vulnerable adult is being abused or neglected — or is neglecting themselves — when that adult cannot seek help on their own?
questions.questionZh: 在 BC 省，当一位弱势成年人遭受虐待或忽视（或自我忽视）、而本人无法自行求助时，由哪个机构被指定接收并处理相关报告？

options.en: The RCMP or municipal police, who hold the sole statutory authority under the Adult Guardianship Act
options.zh: RCMP 或市警，他们依《Adult Guardianship Act》拥有唯一的法定权限

options.en: A designated agency — the regional health authority, Providence Health Care or Community Living BC
options.zh: 指定机构——地区卫生局、Providence Health Care 或 Community Living BC

options.en: The Ministry of Children and Family Development, which covers all vulnerable persons
options.zh: 儿童与家庭发展厅，负责所有弱势人群

options.en: The EMA Licensing Board, through its complaints and investigations process
options.zh: EMA 发牌委员会，通过其投诉与调查程序

questions.explanationEn: Part 3 of BC's Adult Guardianship Act names designated agencies to respond to abuse, neglect and self-neglect of adults who cannot seek support because of a physical restraint, a disability or a condition affecting their decision-making: the five regional health authorities, Providence Health Care and Community Living BC. Anyone may report to a designated agency — reporting is permitted, not mandatory, for the general public — and the agency investigates and arranges support. Police become involved where a crime has occurred or someone is in immediate danger, but they are not the designated agency. The Ministry of Children and Family Development deals with children under the Child, Family and Community Service Act, and the Licensing Board regulates paramedics, not patients.
questions.explanationZh: BC《Adult Guardianship Act》第 3 部分指定了专门机构，处理因身体受限、残疾或影响决策能力的状况而无法自行求助的成年人遭受虐待、忽视或自我忽视的情况：五个地区卫生局、Providence Health Care 和 Community Living BC。任何人都可以向指定机构报告——对公众而言是「可以报告」而非强制——由该机构调查并安排支持。有犯罪发生或有人处于即时危险时警察才介入，但他们不是指定机构。儿童与家庭发展厅依《Child, Family and Community Service Act》处理儿童事务；发牌委员会管的是护理员，不是患者。

questions.questionEn: What is the main role of BCEHS community paramedics?
questions.questionZh: BCEHS 社区护理员（community paramedics）的主要职责是什么？

options.en: Responding to 911 calls in rural communities in place of a regular ambulance crew
options.zh: 在乡村社区代替常规救护车组响应 911 呼叫

options.en: Prescribing and adjusting chronic-disease medications under a physician's standing medical order
options.zh: 在医生的常规医嘱下开具和调整慢性病药物

options.en: Scheduled home visits, health checks, education and referrals in rural and remote communities
options.zh: 在乡村和偏远社区做预约家访、健康检查、健康教育和转介

options.en: Staffing hospital emergency departments during periods of nursing shortage
options.zh: 在护士短缺期间到医院急诊科顶班

questions.explanationEn: BCEHS's community paramedicine program, launched in 2015 and now operating in roughly a hundred rural and remote communities, uses paramedics in a non-emergency role: planned home visits for people with chronic conditions such as heart failure, COPD and diabetes, wellness checks, vital-sign and medication monitoring, health education, and linking patients with primary care and community services. It bridges gaps in access rather than replacing the 911 response, and community paramedics do not prescribe or work as hospital staff. For a 911 crew, knowing the program exists turns a repeat caller with unmet social and health needs into a referral instead of a dead end.
questions.explanationZh: BCEHS 的社区护理员项目于 2015 年启动，目前覆盖大约一百个乡村和偏远社区，让护理员承担非急救角色：为心衰、COPD、糖尿病等慢性病患者做计划内家访，做健康状况巡查，监测生命体征和用药，开展健康教育，并把患者与初级保健和社区服务连接起来。它填补的是可及性的缺口，不是取代 911 响应；社区护理员不开处方，也不在医院当工作人员。对 911 车组来说，知道有这个项目，就能把一个有未满足的社会和健康需求的反复呼叫者变成一次转介，而不是一个死胡同。

questions.questionEn: Over one hot week your crew attends four calls at the same low-income seniors' building for heat-related illness; none of the apartments has air conditioning and the building manager says fans are 'not allowed'. Beyond treating each patient, which action best reflects system-level advocacy?
questions.questionZh: 一周高温天里，你们车组因热相关疾病四次出诊同一栋低收入老年公寓；没有一间公寓有空调，楼宇管理员说风扇「不允许用」。除了治疗每位患者，哪项行动最能体现系统层面的倡导？

options.en: Document the heat and the lack of cooling in every PCR so that the record is complete for any later review
options.zh: 在每份 PCR 中记录高温和缺乏降温条件，确保日后任何审查时记录完整

options.en: Advise each patient to drink more water and to visit a shopping mall during the hottest hours
options.zh: 建议每位患者多喝水，最热的几个小时去商场待着

options.en: Report the pattern to your service and public health so the building can be targeted for cooling checks
options.zh: 把这一规律报告给机构和公共卫生部门，让这栋楼成为降温巡查的重点

options.en: Ask the building manager to post a notice reminding residents to keep their curtains closed
options.zh: 请楼宇管理员贴一张通知，提醒住户拉上窗帘

questions.explanationEn: Four heat calls from one building in a week is a signal about the building, not about four unlucky individuals. BC learned this in the 2021 heat dome, when the Coroners Service counted 619 heat-related deaths — overwhelmingly older adults living alone, indoors, in homes without adequate cooling. Social accountability means moving the information to where it can change conditions: your service's medical or community-health leads and the local public-health unit can arrange welfare checks, cooling-room access and pressure on a landlord whose 'no fans' rule may itself be unlawful. Thorough PCR documentation is necessary and supports the escalation, but by itself it changes nothing. Hydration advice and a trip to the mall help one patient on one day, and a curtain notice is a token gesture against indoor temperatures that killed people.
questions.explanationZh: 一栋楼一周四次热相关出诊，反映的是这栋楼的问题，而不是四个倒霉的个人。BC 在 2021 年「热穹顶」中学到了这一点：验尸官服务统计了 619 例热相关死亡——绝大多数是独居的老年人，死在室内、死在没有足够降温条件的家中。社会问责意味着把信息送到能改变条件的地方：你机构的医疗或社区健康负责人以及当地公共卫生部门可以安排上门探视、开放纳凉场所，并向房东施压——「不许用风扇」的规定本身就可能违法。详尽的 PCR 记录是必要的，也支撑着后续的升级，但它本身改变不了任何事。补水建议和去商场只帮到一位患者一天；贴通知拉窗帘，对已经致人死亡的室内高温来说只是象征性的姿态。
